“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to the notion of a ‘dharma that can rejoice in and dedicate’ toward the dharma that can rejoice in and dedicate, and gives rise to the notion of a ‘dharma that is rejoiced in and dedicated’ toward the dharma that is rejoiced in and dedicated, yet still performs the rejoicing and dedication for the sake of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment—then the mind of rejoicing and dedication generated by this bodhisattva mahāsattva falls into the perversions of notion, mind, and view; all such rejoicing and dedication they generate is erroneous, and the bodhisattva should know how to skillfully distance themselves from it.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva considers all the roots of virtue associated with the *pāramitās* belonging to those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones—who have universally severed the paths of existence and cut off the ways of conceptual proliferation in the present; who, from their first generation of the mind until they realize the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, and continuing through their entry into the realm of *nirvāṇa* without remainder, and even until the extinction of their True Dharma—all the roots of virtue associated with the *pāramitās* of these Buddhas during that interval;
as well as the roots of virtue associated with the *pāramitās* when those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, bestow predictions upon bodhisattvas;"
If the Buddha, the World-Honored One, bestows a prediction upon a pratyekabuddha, it concerns the roots of goodness associated with the contemplation of dependent origination;
if the Buddha, the World-Honored One, bestows a prediction upon a śrāvaka, it concerns the roots of goodness consisting of giving, morality, and cultivation that have been initiated;
and it includes all contaminated and uncontaminated roots of goodness belonging to those in the stage of training (śaikṣa).
If it be the untainted roots of goodness of those in the stage of no-more-learning;

or the Buddha-World-Honored One’s aggregate of ethical discipline, aggregate of meditative concentration, aggregate of wisdom, aggregate of liberation, and aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation;
or great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings;
Whether it be other immeasurable and innumerable Buddha-dharmas;
or the true Dharma proclaimed by the Buddha, the World-Honored One;
or those roots of goodness consisting in diligent cultivation, superior understanding, and firm abiding in that true Dharma;
Whatever roots of goodness planted by various ordinary beings regarding the True Dharma;
whatever roots of goodness planted by devas, nāgas, asuras, and others upon hearing the True Dharma, and even those planted by animals upon hearing the True Dharma;
and whatever roots of goodness planted by humans, devas, and others after the Parinirvāṇa of the Buddha, the World-Honored One.
Having thus gathered and weighed all these together, one should manifest a mind of rejoicing that is most honored, most supreme, most excellent, and most sublime.
Furthermore, taking these various meritorious deeds associated with such rejoicing, one should share them equally with all sentient beings and dedicate them toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

"At such a time, if one correctly understands that all dharmas which can be rejoiced in and dedicated are exhausted, extinguished, detached from, and transformed, then the intrinsic nature of all those dharmas of rejoicing and dedication is empty."
Although one knows in this way, one is able to rejoice and dedicate [the merit] toward unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
Furthermore, at that time, if one correctly understands that there is no dharma whatsoever that can rejoice or dedicate itself to a dharma.
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is empty, and within emptiness there are no phenomena of either agent or object for rejoicing in or dedicating.
Although they know this, they are able to rejoice in and dedicate toward unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment; thus, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not fall into errors of perception, mind, or view.

Why is this? It is because this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward the mind of sympathetic joy (*anumodanā-citta*) or the roots of merit (*kuśalamūla*) that are the object of such joy; nor does he give rise to attachment toward the mind of dedication (*pariṇāmanā-citta*) or the unsurpassed enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*) to which they are dedicated. By being without attachment, he does not fall into error.
The mind of sympathetic joy and dedication thus aroused by a bodhisattva is called the correct, unsurpassed sympathetic joy and dedication; it is far removed from all false conceptualization.

“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva conceives the notion of ‘the dharma that can rejoice in and dedicate’ regarding the dharma that can rejoice in and dedicate, and conceives the notion of ‘the dharma that is rejoiced in and dedicated’ regarding the dharma that is rejoiced in and dedicated, yet still rejoices in and dedicates toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment—then the mind of rejoicing and dedication raised by this bodhisattva mahāsattva falls into the perversions of notion, mind, and view; all such rejoicings and dedications are erroneous, and the bodhisattva should know how to skillfully remain far removed from them.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva considers all the roots of goodness associated with the *pāramitās* belonging to all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the past, future, and present—who have severed the paths of existence and cut off the ways of conceptual proliferation—from their first generation of the mind until they attain the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, and continuing through their successive stages until they enter the realm of *nirupadhiśeṣa-nirvāṇa*, and even until the extinction of their True Dharma;
as well as the roots of goodness associated with the *pāramitās* when those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, bestow predictions upon bodhisattvas; [the bodhisattva should likewise consider these]."
If the Buddha, the World-Honored One, bestows a prediction upon a pratyekabuddha, it concerns the roots of goodness associated with the contemplation of dependent origination;
if the Buddha, the World-Honored One, bestows a prediction upon a śrāvaka, it concerns the roots of goodness consisting of giving, morality, and cultivation that they have initiated;
and all the contaminated and uncontaminated roots of goodness belonging to those in the stage of training (śaikṣa).
If it be the untainted roots of goodness of those in the stage of no-more-learning;
or the Buddha World-Honored One’s aggregate of ethical discipline, aggregate of concentration, aggregate of wisdom, aggregate of liberation, and aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation;
or great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings;
If there are other immeasurable and innumerable Buddha-dharmas;
if the Buddha, the World-Honored One, proclaims the True Dharma;
or if one diligently cultivates, trains in, gains resolute understanding of, and dwells in those roots of goodness regarding the True Dharma;
Whatever roots of goodness are planted by ordinary beings within the True Dharma;
whatever roots of goodness are planted by devas, nāgas, asuras, and others upon hearing the True Dharma, and even those planted by animals upon hearing the True Dharma;
and whatever roots of goodness are planted by humans, devas, and others after the Parinirvāṇa of the Buddha, the World-Honored One.
Having thus gathered and weighed all these together, one should manifest a mind of sympathetic joy that is most honored, most supreme, most excellent, and most sublime.

Furthermore, one should take these various meritorious deeds accompanied by such sympathetic joy and, sharing them equally with all sentient beings, dedicate them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

"At such a time, if one correctly understands that all phenomena which can be rejoiced in and dedicated are exhausted, extinguished, departed from, and transformed, then the intrinsic nature of all those phenomena of rejoicing and dedication is empty."
Although they know this, they are able to rejoice in merit and dedicate it toward unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
Furthermore, at that time, they correctly understand that there is no dharma whatsoever that can be rejoiced in or dedicated as a dharma.

Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of all phenomena is empty, and within emptiness there are no phenomena whatsoever that can act as the agent or object of rejoicing and dedication.

Although they know this, they are still able to rejoice and dedicate toward unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment; thus, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not fall into errors of perception, mind, or view.

Why is this? It is because this bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not give rise to attachment toward the mind of sympathetic joy (*anumodanā*) or the roots of merit (*kuśalamūla*) that are the object of such joy; nor do they give rise to attachment toward the mind of dedication (*pariṇāmanā*) or the unsurpassed enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*) to which it is dedicated. By virtue of this non-attachment, they do not fall into perversion (*viparyāsa*).
The mind of sympathetic joy and dedication thus aroused by a bodhisattva is called the correct and unsurpassed dedication of sympathetic joy; it is far removed from all false conceptualization.

“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, regarding the phenomena that can be rejoiced in and dedicated, gives rise to the perception of phenomena that can be rejoiced in and dedicated; and regarding the phenomena that are rejoiced in and dedicated, gives rise to the perception of phenomena that are rejoiced in and dedicated, yet still performs the rejoicing and dedication toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment—then the mind of rejoicing and dedication produced by this bodhisattva mahāsattva falls into the perversions of perception, mind, and view. All such rejoicings and dedications are erroneous; the bodhisattva should know how to skillfully distance themselves from them.”
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, regarding the various meritorious deeds they have performed, understands them as being truly secluded and tranquil; and regarding the mind that rejoices in and dedicates [the merit], also understands it as being truly secluded and tranquil."

Having understood this, one practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, remaining entirely without grasping or attachment toward any phenomena, while generating sympathetic joy (*anumodanā*) and dedicating [the merit] toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*). The mind of sympathetic joy and dedication thus generated by this bodhisattva mahāsattva does not fall into the perversions of perception, mind, or view.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, regarding the various meritorious deeds they have cultivated, does not know them as they truly are in their detachment from tranquility, and likewise cannot know the mind that rejoices in and dedicates those merits as being detached from tranquility, yet clings to the signs of all phenomena while giving rise to rejoicing and dedication toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment—then the mind of rejoicing and dedication produced by that bodhisattva mahāsattva falls into the perversions of perception, mind, and view.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to generate a mind of sympathetic joy and dedicate toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment the merits and roots of goodness of the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, who have already entered parinirvāṇa, as well as their disciples, they should form this thought:
'Just as the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, and their disciples have all already entered parinirvāṇa and are non-existent by their very nature, so too are their merits and roots of goodness.'"

The mind that I have generated for sympathetic rejoicing and dedication toward unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, as well as the unsurpassed enlightenment toward which it is dedicated, are likewise in their nature and characteristics entirely unapprehendable.

Having understood this, one generates sympathetic joy toward all roots of goodness and dedicates them to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment; thus, one is able to avoid giving rise to errors of perception, mind, or view, which is called "right sympathetic joy and dedication toward enlightenment."

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva, employing the method of grasping at signs, practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā* by grasping at signs when rejoicing in the roots of virtue and merit of Buddhas and their disciples who have already entered parinirvāṇa, and dedicates this toward awakening, this is not a skillful dedication through rejoicing; by means of this, they fall into the perversions of perception, mind, and view.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, employing the skillful means of non-apprehension of signs, practices the profound perfection of wisdom and, regarding the roots of goodness and merit of the Buddhas and their disciples who have already entered parinirvāṇa, rejoices in them with detachment from signs and dedicates them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, this is called "skillful rejoicing and dedication. By means of this, one does not fall into the perversions of perception, mind, or view.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya asked the Venerable Subhūti:
"Virtuous One!

How is it that a bodhisattva mahāsattva, without apprehending any signs regarding the roots of goodness, the merits, and the meritorious deeds associated with rejoicing performed by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and their assemblies of disciples, is nevertheless able to rejoice and dedicate [the merit] toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?"

Subhūti replied, “It should be known that the Prajñāpāramitā in which Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas train possesses such skillful means (upāya-kauśalya) that, although they do not grasp at signs, their activities are accomplished; indeed, apart from the Prajñāpāramitā, there is no way to correctly generate sympathetic joy (anumodanā) and perform the dedication (pariṇāmanā).”
Therefore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who wish to accomplish what is to be done should study the perfection of wisdom.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya said:
“Venerable Subhūti!
Do not speak thus. Why is this?

Because within the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, along with their assemblies of disciples and the roots of merit and wholesome qualities they have accomplished, are all non-existent and utterly unattainable; likewise, the various meritorious deeds performed with sympathetic joy and the generation of the mind dedicated toward unsurpassed enlightenment are also non-existent and utterly unattainable.
"In this regard, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they should contemplate in this way:

'The nature of the merits and roots of goodness of the Buddhas of the past and their assemblies of disciples has already ceased; the nature of the meritorious deeds performed with sympathetic joy and the resolve for dedication toward unsurpassed enlightenment has also become utterly quiescent.'"

If I were to apprehend signs and engage in conceptual discrimination regarding the roots of virtue and merits of those Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, and their assemblies of disciples; or if I were to apprehend signs and engage in conceptual discrimination regarding the various meritorious deeds accompanied by sympathetic joy and the resolve for dedication toward unsurpassed enlightenment—then, by means of such expedients of apprehending signs and conceptual discrimination, to generate sympathetic joy and dedicate [the merit] toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, would be disapproved by all the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones.

Why is this? To grasp at signs and engage in conceptual discrimination regarding the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, and their disciples who have already entered parinirvāṇa, and then to rejoice and dedicate [the merit] toward unsurpassed bodhi—this is called having great attainment.
The past has already ceased and is non-existent; therefore, the future and present disciples of the Buddha have not yet arrived and do not abide, and they likewise cannot be apprehended.

If that which is unobtainable is not an object of grasping at signs, yet one grasps at its signs and gives rise to sympathetic joy (anumodanā) dedicated toward enlightenment (bodhi-pariṇāmanā), one falls into perversion.

If there is loss of mindfulness and one grasps at signs, know that this is not a skillful sympathetic joy or dedication; rather, it must be without grasping at signs and without conceptual discrimination to be called skillful sympathetic joy and dedication.

"Therefore, the assembly of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should train in the skillful means of the Prajñāpāramitā; by the power of these skillful means, they are able to correctly generate sympathetic joy and dedication."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to study such skillful means, they should repeatedly hear, receive, uphold, read, and recite the Prajñāpāramitā; they should master it thoroughly, reflect upon it according to the principle, and diligently inquire of their teacher regarding its profound meaning and intent.
Why is this? If one does not rely upon the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, one will ultimately be unable to attain skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*).
Without such skillful means, it is impossible to correctly generate sympathetic joy (*anumodanā*) and dedication (*pariṇāmanā*).

Why is this? Because when one takes up signs and engages in conceptual discrimination regarding the various merits of the Buddhas of the past and their assemblies of disciples, and then rejoices in them and dedicates [the merit], the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, do not approve of such rejoicing.

"Therefore, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas wish to correctly generate sympathetic joy toward and dedicate the roots of goodness and merit of all Buddhas and their disciples toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, they should not, within that process, give rise to conceptualizations of grasping at signs based on the apprehension of something existing."

If, within this, one gives rise to conceptualization that grasps at signs and apprehends something as real, and then rejoices and dedicates [the merit], the Buddha does not say that such a person possesses great benefit. Why is this?
Such a mind of sympathetic joy and dedication is called "mixed with poison" because it involves false conceptualization.

It is like food that, though possessing excellent color, fragrance, and flavor, is mixed with poisonous medicine; a person of shallow understanding greedily seizes and eats it. Although it may initially satisfy the mind with joy and happiness, once the food is digested, one undergoes manifold sufferings, or even dies, or nearly loses one's life.

"In this way, a certain class of individuals, having poorly grasped and poorly examined the words and meanings of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and having poorly recited and poorly mastered its profound significance, says to those of the Mahāyāna lineage:
'Come!'"
"Good son!

Regarding the aggregates of morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones of the past, future, and present; as well as their other immeasurable and boundless merits;
and whatever roots of goodness Buddhist disciples have planted in the presence of those Buddhas—"
Whatever roots of goodness have been planted by those bodhisattvas when the Buddha, the World-Honored One, bestowed upon them the prediction of unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment;
whatever roots of goodness have been planted by those sentient beings when the Buddha, the World-Honored One, bestowed predictions upon the pratyekabuddhas and śrāvakas;
and whatever roots of goodness have been planted by devas, humans, asuras, and others in the presence of the Buddhas until the True Dharma has not yet been extinguished—
Whatever roots of goodness have been planted by sons and daughters of good family, as well as the roots of goodness arising from rejoicing in and dedicating the merit accomplished by others.

Having thus gathered and weighed all these together, one rejoices in their presence and dedicates them equally in common with all sentient beings toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"The rejoicing and dedication thus described employ the conceptualization of signs and the grasping for attainments as their means.
Just as worldly food mixed with poison is beneficial at first but harmful in the end, this is not a wholesome rejoicing or dedication."

Why is this? Because those who grasp at signs through the apprehension of something to be attained and give rise to a mind of sympathetic joy and dedication that is mixed with poison, their actions are defiled.
A person belonging to the bodhisattva lineage should not train according to what they have said.
"Therefore, O Great Virtuous One!

You should explain how sons of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva Vehicle should rejoice in and dedicate the roots of goodness and merit of all Buddhas and their disciples throughout the three times and ten directions; how can this be called the 'poison-free, wondrously virtuous rejoicing and dedication'?"
The Venerable Subhūti replied to Maitreya:

“Sons of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle and practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, wishing not to misrepresent the Buddha when they give rise to a mind of sympathetic joy (*anumodanā*) and dedication (*pariṇāmanā*), should form this thought:

‘Just as the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, with their unobstructed Buddha-eye, have thoroughly realized and fully known that these roots of virtue and wholesome qualities possess such a nature, such characteristics, and such a dharma that they may be sympathetically rejoiced in; so too should I now likewise rejoice.’”

Just as the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, with their unobstructed Buddha-eye, have thoroughly realized and fully known how these various bases of meritorious action should be dedicated toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, so too shall I now dedicate them in this same way.

"Those sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle should, regarding the roots of virtue and merit of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and their disciples, perform such rejoicing and dedication."
If one performs such sympathetic joy and dedication, one does not slander the Buddhas; all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, likewise rejoice in it.

This mind of sympathetic joy and dedication of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is unmixed with any poison and free from all faults; it is called "correct" and "wholesome" sympathetic joy and dedication. It accords with the true Dharma-realm, and both its aspiration and its resolute conviction are perfectly fulfilled.
"Furthermore, Great Being!

Those sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle and practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā* should perform this rejoicing and dedication regarding the roots of virtue and merits of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and their disciples:

'Just as the Buddha’s aggregate of ethical discipline, aggregate of concentration, aggregate of wisdom, aggregate of liberation, aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation, and all other dharmas do not fall within the three realms and are not subsumed by the three periods of time, so too should this rejoicing and dedication be performed.'"

Why is this? Because those dharmas are empty of intrinsic nature (*svabhāva-śūnya*), they do not fall within the three realms nor are they subsumed within the three periods of time; the same applies to sympathetic joy and dedication.
This means that because the intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of all Tathāgatas is empty, they do not fall within the three realms and are not subsumed by the three periods of time;
because the intrinsic nature of the merits of all Buddhas is empty, they do not fall within the three realms and are not subsumed by the three periods of time;
and because the intrinsic nature of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, humans, devas, and so forth is empty, they do not fall within the three realms and are not subsumed by the three periods of time.
Because those roots of goodness are empty of intrinsic nature, they do not fall within the three realms and are not subsumed by the three times;
because that sympathetic joy is empty of intrinsic nature, it does not fall within the three realms and is not subsumed by the three times;
because the phenomena to which they are dedicated are empty of intrinsic nature, they do not fall within the three realms and are not subsumed by the three times.
Because that which is capable of dedication is empty of intrinsic nature, it does not fall within the three realms and is not subsumed by the three periods of time.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they understand the nature and characteristics of all phenomena as they truly are, and thus do not fall within the three realms and are not subsumed by the three periods of time.

If one does not fall into the three realms and is not subsumed by the three periods of time, then one cannot employ the sign of existence as a means or the apprehension of something to be attained as a means to generate sympathetic joy and dedicate it toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Why is this? Because all phenomena are by nature unarisen;

if a phenomenon is unarisen, it is non-existent. One cannot rejoice in or dedicate that which is a non-existent phenomenon, because it is non-existent. When a bodhisattva mahāsattva thus rejoices and dedicates toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment—unmixed with any poisons, indestructible, without falling into extremes, without grasping, and in accordance with the true dharma-realm—it is called the Great Dedication, which is ultimately perfect and complete.

“Sons and daughters of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle, if they employ the method of signs or the method of apprehension when generating a mind of sympathetic joy and dedication toward the roots of goodness and merit of the Tathāgatas and their disciples, you should know that this is a perverted sympathetic joy and dedication.”
This mind of wrong sympathetic joy and dedication is not praised by the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, while practicing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, forms this thought:

"Just as all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas in the realms of the ten directions have truly realized the roots of virtue and wholesome qualities through their dharmas, and as there are such dharmas upon which one may rely to give rise to unerring sympathetic joy and dedication..."

I should now likewise, in reliance upon such dharmas, give rise to sympathetic joy and dedicate it toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; this is the correct generation of sympathetic joy and dedication.
"By means of this, he will certainly realize unexcelled bodhi, turn the wondrous wheel of Dharma, and benefit all beings.
At that time, the World-Honored One praised Subhūti, saying:
"Excellent!"
Excellent!
You are now able to perform great Buddha-work for the sake of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. Why is this so?

For you, as a bodhisattva mahāsattva, have proclaimed the unerring sympathetic rejoicing and dedication, just as all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas—having thoroughly realized and fully known all roots of virtue and so forth—possess such a nature, such characteristics, and such qualities that they give rise to unerring sympathetic rejoicing and dedication.
"This mind of sympathetic joy and dedication is commensurate with the true Dharma-realm and is ultimately perfect and complete; you are now able to explain it according to reality.
Subhūti, you should know this!"

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to use skillful means to teach and transform sentient beings in as many trichiliocosm worlds as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, causing them all to dwell securely in the ten paths of wholesome action, the merit obtained from this would be surpassed by the merit of a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s arising of non-erroneous sympathetic joy and dedication; it is the most excellent, the most superior, the most noble, the most lofty, the most wondrous, the most subtle, the highest, the unsurpassed, the unequaled, and the equal to the unequaled.
"Furthermore, Subhūti! Let us set aside for a moment the matter of establishing [beings] in the ten paths of wholesome action.

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to skillfully convert sentient beings in as many trichiliocosm worlds as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, causing them all to dwell securely in the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the five supernormal powers—the merit obtained from this would be surpassed by the merit of a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s unerring rejoicing and dedication; it would be the most excellent, the most supreme, the most honored, the most sublime, the most wondrous, the most exquisite, the highest, and the unsurpassed, being peerless and equal to the unequaled."
"Furthermore, Subhūti! Let alone causing them to abide in the four dhyānas and so forth.

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to use skillful means to teach and transform sentient beings in as many trichiliocosm worlds as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, causing them all to abide in the fruit of a stream-enterer, or the fruit of a once-returner, or the fruit of a non-returner, or the fruit of an arhat, or in the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha—the merit obtained thereby would be surpassed by the merit of a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s unerring rejoicing and dedication; compared to that [former] merit, it is the most supreme, the most excellent, the most honored, the highest, the most wondrous, the most subtle, the most superior, the unsurpassed, the unequaled, and the equal to the unequaled."
"Furthermore, Subhūti! Let us set aside [the merit of] causing others to abide in the fruit of a stream-enterer and so forth.

Suppose all sentient beings in as many trichiliocosm worlds as there are grains of sand in the Ganges were each to attain the merits of the fruits of a stream-enterer, once-returner, non-returner, arhat, and the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; compared to those merits, the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s arising of unerring rejoicing and dedication is the most supreme, the most excellent, the most honored, the highest, the most sublime, the most exquisite, the most superior, the unsurpassed, the unequaled, and the equal to the unequaled."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Let alone all such merits as those of the fruit of stream-entry and so forth.

Suppose that all sentient beings in as many trichiliocosm great thousandfold world systems as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River in the ten directions were to each give rise to the mind set on unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

Suppose there were sentient beings in as many trichiliocosm world-systems as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River in the ten directions, and each of them were to provide the Bodhisattvas with the finest garments, food and drink, bedding, medicine, and immeasurable varieties of exquisite articles of pleasure for as many great eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges, using the method of "grasping at attainments" to make offerings, pay homage, revere, and praise them—what do you think?
“By this cause and condition, would these sentient beings acquire much merit?
Subhūti replied, “Very much!”
"World-Honored One!
It is very much so! Sugata!"
“If this mass of merit were to have a physical form, the worlds in each of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, would not be able to contain it.
The Buddha told Subhūti: “It is so! It is so!”
"So it is! It is just as you have said.

If sons and daughters of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle should generate unerring sympathetic joy and dedicate the roots of virtue of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and their disciples, the merit they obtain will be far greater than the former—immeasurable, incalculable, beyond all calculation, analogy, or comparison."

Why is this so? Because the unerring rejoicing and dedication generated by these sons of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle are embraced by the skillful means of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* through the method of non-apprehension; they accord with the *dharmadhātu* and are thus supreme and peerless.

The mass of merit obtained by those sentient beings, because it is based on the method of apprehending something as real, does not approach even a hundredth part of this rejoicing and dedication that has arisen; it does not approach a thousandth part, nor even a *upaniṣad* (infinitesimal) part.
At that time, the Four Great Heavenly Kings, each accompanied by a retinue of twenty thousand devaputras, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, joined their palms in reverence, and addressed him, saying:
“World-Honored One!

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva’s arousal of non-erroneous sympathetic joy and dedication is embraced by the skillful means of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, employing the method of non-apprehension, its power is vast and equal to the true *dharmadhātu*. It can swiftly realize the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*), and it is infinitely superior to the aforementioned giving performed with apprehension, such that no comparison can be made between them.

At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, up to the King of the Heaven of Making Use of Others' Transformations, each accompanied by a retinue of one hundred thousand devaputras, all carrying various celestial and exquisite flower garlands, powdered and scattered incenses, robes, necklaces, precious banners, pennants, canopies, and many wonderful and rare treasures, played celestial music as offerings to the Buddha. With worship, reverence, respect, and praise, they prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, joined their palms, and addressed him, saying:

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva’s arising of non-erroneous rejoicing and dedication is characterized by non-apprehension as the skillful means and is embraced by the skillful means of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, its power is vast and equal to the true *dharmadhātu*. It can swiftly realize the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*), and it is infinitely superior to the aforementioned giving based on apprehension, such that no comparison can be made.

At that time, the Great Brahmā, and so forth up to the gods of the Akaniṣṭha Heaven, each accompanied by immeasurable hundreds of thousands of celestial hosts, approached the place where the Buddha was, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, joined their palms in reverence, and together cried out:
“How marvelous! How rare!”
“World-Honored One!
How extraordinary!
Well-Gone One!”

Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva’s arousal of non-erroneous rejoicing and dedication is performed by means of non-apprehension and is embraced by the skillful means of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, its power is vast and equal to the true *dharmadhātu*. It can swiftly realize the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*), and it is infinitely superior—beyond comparison—to the aforementioned giving that involves apprehension.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll 543; The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra,
Scroll 544.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
The Fourth Division, Chapter Six: Rejoicing and Dedication, Part Two. At that time, the Buddha addressed the assembly of devas, including those from the Śuddhāvāsa Heavens, saying:

"Let us set aside for a moment the case of all sentient beings in as many trichiliocosm world-systems as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River in the ten directions, all of whom have resolved to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

Suppose all sentient beings in the infinite worlds of the ten directions were to generate the mind of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; and suppose that every single one of those sentient beings were to take excellent garments, food and drink, bedding, medicine, and immeasurable kinds of superior articles of pleasure, and for as many great eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, were to provide offerings, honor, respect, and praise toward those bodhisattvas by means of the practice of "grasping at attainment."

If sons and daughters of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle were to generate unerring sympathetic joy toward the roots of virtue and merit of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and their disciples, and dedicate those merits, the merit obtained would be far greater than the former—immeasurable, incalculable, beyond all calculation, analogy, or comparison.

Why is this? Because the unerring rejoicing and dedication generated by these sons of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle are embraced by the skillful means of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* through the method of non-apprehension; and because they accord with the *dharmadhātu*, they are supreme and peerless.

The mass of merit obtained by those sentient beings, because it is accomplished through the method of apprehension, does not equal even one hundredth part, nor one thousandth part, nor even an *upaniṣad* part of this rejoicing and dedication that has been generated here.
“O devas, you should know!
Let this matter stand aside for a moment.

Suppose that all sentient beings in as many trichiliocosm world-systems as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River in the ten directions were to each give rise to the mind of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; and suppose they were to universally rejoice in and dedicate toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment—by means of the conceptual signs and the apprehension of objects—all the aggregates of morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation belonging to all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past, future, and present, as well as all other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-dharmas, the roots of goodness of all their disciples, and the roots of goodness already accumulated, yet to be accumulated, or currently being accumulated by other sentient beings, having gathered and weighed them all together. What do you think?”

If sons of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle have set out for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they universally gather together and weigh all the aggregates of morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation, as well as the other immeasurable and boundless buddha-dharmas of all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past, future, and present; they likewise gather together and weigh all the roots of goodness of their disciples, and all the roots of goodness of other sentient beings that have been accumulated, will be accumulated, or are being accumulated in the present. Having thus collected and weighed all these, they manifest before them the performance of meritorious deeds accompanied by rejoicing—rejoicing that is most honored, most supreme, most excellent, most sublime, inconceivable, immeasurable, unsurpassed, and peerless.

Furthermore, taking these various meritorious deeds accompanied by such sympathetic joy, one shares them equally with all sentient beings and dedicates them toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. This arising of sympathetic joy and dedication is a hundred times superior, a thousand times superior, and even up to an *upaniṣad*-fold superior to the previously mentioned arising of sympathetic joy and dedication.

Why is this? It is because this arising of rejoicing and dedication is characterized by signlessness and non-attainment as its skillful means, whereas that previously arisen rejoicing and dedication was characterized by signs and attainment as its skillful means.
At that time, Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:

“As the Blessed One has said, if sons of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle set out for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they universally gather together and weigh all the roots of virtue and merit of all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and their disciples of the past, future, and present; they then manifest before them all manner of meritorious deeds accompanied by sympathetic joy—most honored, most supreme, most excellent, most subtle, inconceivable, immeasurable, unsurpassed, and unequaled.”

Furthermore, taking these various meritorious deeds accompanied by sympathetic joy, one shares them equally with all sentient beings and dedicates them toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. This arising of sympathetic joy and dedication is superior to the previous arising of sympathetic joy and dedication by even more than an *upaniṣad* multiple.
"Bhagavān!
To what extent can it be said that the subsequent rejoicing and dedication surpasses the preceding rejoicing and dedication, even by a factor of *upaniṣad*?"

The Buddha told Subhūti: “These sons of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle do not grasp at nor reject, do not prize nor despise, the dharmas of the three times. They neither obtain anything nor fail to obtain anything; they have no conceptualization and no differentiated conceptualization; they have nothing to perceive and no subsequent perception. They contemplate these dharmas as all being accumulations of conceptualization, and they penetrate that all dharmas are without arising and without cessation, without going and without coming, without gathering and without dispersing, without entering and without exiting:

‘In this, there is no dharma that has arisen, will arise, or is presently arising, nor is there any dharma that has ceased, will cease, or is presently ceasing. I should, in accordance with the true suchness and the dharma-realm of dharmas, by means of non-attainment as a skillful method, generate sympathetic joy and dedicate it toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.’”

"Subhūti, you should know that this arising of rejoicing and dedication surpasses the previous arising of rejoicing and dedication based on the perception of something obtainable and the view of something obtainable, even by a multiple of upaniṣad."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Sons of good family and others who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle, wishing to generate unerring sympathetic joy and dedication toward the roots of virtue associated with the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom belonging to the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, and their disciples of the past, future, and present, should form this thought:
'Just as true liberation is, so too is generosity;'"
As true liberation is, so too is pure ethical discipline;
as true liberation is, so too is patience;
as true liberation is, so too is diligence.
As true liberation is, so too is meditative concentration;
as true liberation is, so too is wisdom;

as true liberation is, so too are the aggregate of ethical discipline, the aggregate of concentration, the aggregate of wisdom, the aggregate of liberation, and the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation.
As is true liberation, so too is sympathetic joy;
as is true liberation, so too are all meritorious deeds accompanied by sympathetic joy;
as is true liberation, so too are the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and the Pratyekabuddhas.
Just as true liberation is, so too are the śrāvakas who have already entered parinirvāṇa;
just as true liberation is, so too are all dharmas of the past that have already ceased;
just as true liberation is, so too are all dharmas of the future that have not yet arisen.
As true liberation is, so too are all phenomena currently manifesting;
as true liberation is, so too were the disciples of the Buddhas of the past;
as true liberation is, so too will be the disciples of the Buddhas of the future.
Just as true liberation is, so too are the disciples of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in the infinite, incalculable, and boundless worlds of the ten directions in the present;
just as true liberation is, so too are all meritorious qualities and roots of goodness;
just as the nature of all phenomena is without bondage or liberation, without defilement or purity, without arising or exhaustion, without birth or cessation, and without grasping or relinquishing.

I rejoice in these roots of virtue and merit as they manifest before me; I share these roots of virtue equally with all sentient beings and dedicate them toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, employing as my means the non-transference, the non-destruction, the signless, and the non-attainment.
Such rejoicing and dedication are not capable of rejoicing or dedicating, because there is nothing to rejoice in and nothing to which one dedicates.
Such rejoicing and dedication that arise are neither proceeding nor ceasing, because they are without arising or cessation.

"Subhūti, you should know that the unerring rejoicing and dedication performed by these sons of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle surpasses the rejoicing and dedication with signs and attainment previously performed, even by a factor of *upaniṣad*."
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such rejoicing and dedication, they will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!..."

Suppose that all sentient beings in as many trichiliocosm great thousandfold world systems as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River were to each give rise to the mind of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, set out toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete bodhi, and skillfully practice the conduct of a bodhisattva through expedient means.

Furthermore, suppose there were sentient beings in as many trichiliocosm great thousandfold world systems in the ten directions as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, all of whom were to give rise to the mind of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and set out toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete bodhi.

Each of these bodhisattvas, toward all those other bodhisattva assemblies, provides superior and exquisite clothing, food and drink, bedding, medicine, and immeasurable kinds of excellent articles of pleasure for as many great eons as there are sands in the Ganges, using the method of "having something to be attained" to offer worship, respect, honor, and praise.
"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being embraced by the skillful means of the profound perfection of wisdom,

universally [dedicates] all the aggregates of morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation belonging to the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the past, future, and present; or those of the solitary..."
One awakens to all the aggregates of morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation;
as well as the aggregates of morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation possessed by all śrāvakas;
and the three types of meritorious action consisting of giving, morality, and cultivation performed by other sentient beings.
Having thus gathered and weighed all these matters together, one manifests before oneself those meritorious deeds accompanied by sympathetic joy—
most honored and supreme, most excellent and sublime, inconceivable, immeasurable, unsurpassed, and peerless.

Furthermore, taking these various meritorious deeds accompanied by such sympathetic joy, he shares them equally with all sentient beings and dedicates them toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Subhūti, you should know that such meritorious deeds of a bodhisattva,

consisting of rejoicing and dedication, surpass by a hundredfold, a thousandfold, and even up to an *upaniṣad*-fold the meritorious deeds associated with giving performed by the aforementioned bodhisattvas who employ the method of apprehending something as real.

Why is this? Because while those bodhisattvas perform various meritorious deeds associated with giving by employing the method of apprehending something, these bodhisattvas employ the method of non-apprehension when they rejoice and dedicate [their merit].
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Let alone the sentient beings in as many trichiliocosm great thousandfold world systems as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, all of whom have resolved to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening and have set out toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete bodhi; let us consider the various meritorious deeds associated with giving performed by the assembly of bodhisattvas, employing the method of 'having something to be attained' as their skillful means."

Suppose that all sentient beings in as many trichiliocosm worlds as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River in the ten directions were to each resolve upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment and set out toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete bodhi; and suppose these bodhisattvas each remained for as many great eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, cultivating sublime conduct of body, sublime conduct of speech, and sublime conduct of mind, while upholding pure ethical discipline by means of the method of apprehending something to be attained.
“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being embraced by skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*) in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*,

[dedicates] all the aggregates of ethical discipline, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation belonging to all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the past, future, and present; or those belonging to the various solitary [buddhas]...”
One realizes all the aggregates of morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation;
as well as the aggregates of morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation possessed by all śrāvakas;
and the three types of meritorious action consisting of giving, morality, and cultivation performed by other sentient beings.
Having thus gathered and weighed all these matters together, one presently initiates those meritorious deeds accompanied by sympathetic joy that are most venerable,
most excellent, supreme, most sublime, inconceivable, immeasurable, unsurpassed, and peerless.

Furthermore, taking these various meritorious deeds accompanied by such sympathetic joy, he shares them equally with all sentient beings and dedicates them toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Subhūti, you should know that the merit resulting from such a bodhisattva’s rejoicing and dedication of all meritorious deeds surpasses by a hundredfold, a thousandfold, and even up to an *upaniṣad*-fold the meritorious deeds associated with pure ethical discipline performed by the aforementioned bodhisattvas who employ the method of apprehending something as real.

Why is this? Because those bodhisattvas perform various meritorious deeds in conjunction with pure ethical discipline by employing the method of apprehending something, whereas these bodhisattvas' sympathetic rejoicing and dedication employ the method of non-apprehension.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Let alone the sentient beings in as many trichiliocosm great thousandfold world systems as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, all of whom have resolved to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and are proceeding toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete bodhi; let us consider the various meritorious deeds associated with pure ethical discipline performed by the assembly of bodhisattvas, using the method of 'apprehending something' as their expedient means."

Suppose that all sentient beings in as many trichiliocosm worlds as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River in the ten directions were to each give rise to the mind of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and set out toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete bodhi; and suppose these bodhisattvas were each to remain for as many great eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges, constantly enduring being reviled, insulted, and harmed by blades and staves from sentient beings in as many trichiliocosm worlds as there are grains of sand in the Ganges throughout the ten directions, practicing patience through the expedient means of "apprehending an object."
“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being sustained by skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*) in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*,

universally [takes as their object] all the aggregates of morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation belonging to the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the past, future, and present; or those belonging to the solitary [buddhas]...”
One awakens to all the aggregates of ethical discipline, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation;
as well as the aggregates of ethical discipline, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation possessed by all śrāvakas;
and the three types of meritorious action consisting of generosity, ethical discipline, and cultivation belonging to other sentient beings.
Having thus gathered and weighed all these matters together, one brings forth before oneself those meritorious deeds accompanied by sympathetic joy that are most honored,
most excellent, supreme, most sublime, inconceivable, immeasurable, unsurpassed, and peerless.

Furthermore, taking these various meritorious deeds accompanied by such sympathetic joy, they share them equally with all sentient beings and dedicate them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Subhūti, you should know that such meritorious deeds of rejoicing and dedication by a bodhisattva surpass the meritorious deeds associated with patience practiced by the aforementioned bodhisattvas who employ the means of apprehending [phenomena] as real, by a factor of a hundred, a thousand, and even up to an *upaniṣad* (an infinitely greater) multiple.

Why is this? Because those bodhisattvas perform various meritorious deeds accompanied by patience using the approach of apprehending something, whereas these bodhisattvas' sympathetic joy and dedication are performed using the approach of non-apprehension.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Let alone the sentient beings in as many trichiliocosm world systems as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River in the ten directions, all of whom have resolved upon unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and are advancing toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, and who perform various meritorious deeds accompanied by patience, employing the method of 'having something to be apprehended. "

Suppose that all sentient beings in as many trichiliocosm worlds as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River in the ten directions were to each give rise to the mind of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and set out toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete bodhi; and suppose these bodhisattvas were each to dwell for as many great eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, neither sitting nor lying down and never sleeping, practicing and undertaking diligence with the method of "having something to be attained."
"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being embraced by the skillful means of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*,

universally [takes as their object] all the aggregates of morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation belonging to the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the past, future, and present; or those of the pratyekabuddhas..."
He realizes all the aggregates of morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation;
as well as the aggregates of morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation possessed by all śrāvakas;
and the three types of meritorious action consisting of giving, morality, and cultivation performed by other sentient beings.
Having thus gathered and weighed all these matters together, one brings forth before oneself those meritorious deeds accompanied by sympathetic joy that are most venerable,
most excellent, supreme, most sublime, inconceivable, immeasurable, unsurpassed, and peerless.

Furthermore, taking these various meritorious deeds associated with sympathetic joy, he shares them equally with all sentient beings and dedicates them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Subhūti, you should know that these meritorious deeds of rejoicing and dedication performed by such bodhisattvas surpass by a hundredfold, a thousandfold, and even up to an *upaniṣad*-fold the meritorious deeds previously described, which were performed by other bodhisattvas through the application of skillful means while still characterized by the apprehension of objects (*upalambha*).

Why is this? Because those bodhisattvas perform various meritorious deeds accompanied by diligence by means of apprehending something, whereas these bodhisattvas’ sympathetic joy and dedication are performed by means of non-apprehension.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Let alone the sentient beings in as many trichiliocosm worlds as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River in the ten directions, all of whom have resolved to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and are proceeding toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete bodhi, and who perform various meritorious deeds accompanied by diligence, using the method of 'apprehending existence' (upalambha).'"

Suppose that all sentient beings in as many trichiliocosm world-systems as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River in the ten directions were to each give rise to the mind of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening and set out toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; and suppose these bodhisattvas were each to dwell for as many great eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, remaining with their minds free from distraction and fixed on a single object, yet practicing meditative concentration by means of the method of apprehending something to be attained.
"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being embraced by skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*) within the profound *prajñāpāramitā*,

[dedicates] all the aggregates of morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation belonging to the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the past, future, and present— and likewise those of the solitary..."
He fully awakens to the aggregate of morality, the aggregate of concentration, the aggregate of wisdom, the aggregate of liberation, and the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation;
he fully awakens to whatever aggregates of morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and knowledge and vision of liberation belong to the śrāvakas;
and he fully awakens to the three types of meritorious action consisting of generosity, morality, and cultivation belonging to other sentient beings.
Having thus gathered and weighed all these matters together, one manifests before oneself those meritorious deeds accompanied by sympathetic joy that are most honored and supreme,
most excellent and sublime, inconceivable, immeasurable, unsurpassed, and peerless.

Furthermore, taking these various meritorious deeds accompanied by such sympathetic joy, he shares them equally with all sentient beings and dedicates them toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Subhūti, you should know that such meritorious deeds of rejoicing and dedication performed by a bodhisattva surpass those previously mentioned meritorious deeds associated with meditative concentration— performed by other bodhisattvas using the method of apprehending something real— by a hundredfold, a thousandfold, and even up to an *upaniṣad*-fold.

Why is this? Because while those bodhisattvas perform various meritorious deeds associated with meditative concentration by employing the method of apprehending something, these bodhisattvas' sympathetic joy and dedication employ the method of non-apprehension.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

Let alone the sentient beings in as many trichiliocosm great thousandfold world systems as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, all of whom have resolved to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and have set out toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening; let us consider the various meritorious deeds associated with meditative concentration performed by those bodhisattvas, using the method of 'apprehending an object' as their skillful means."

Suppose that all sentient beings in as many trichiliocosm world-systems as there are grains of sand in the Ganges in the ten directions were to each give rise to the mind of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and set out toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete bodhi; and suppose these bodhisattvas were each to dwell for as many great eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges, contemplating and examining the nature and characteristics of all phenomena, employing the method of apprehending something as they practice the perfection of wisdom and other roots of virtue.
"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, being embraced by the skillful means of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*,

[dedicates] all the aggregates of morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation belonging to the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the past, future, and present, as well as those of the various pratyekabuddhas..."
He realizes all the aggregates of virtue, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation;
as well as the aggregates of virtue, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation belonging to all śrāvakas;
and the three types of meritorious action consisting of giving, virtue, and cultivation belonging to other sentient beings.
Having thus gathered and weighed all these matters together, one manifests before oneself those meritorious deeds accompanied by sympathetic joy that are most honored and supreme,
most excellent and sublime, inconceivable, immeasurable, unsurpassed, and peerless.

Furthermore, taking these various meritorious deeds accompanied by such sympathetic joy, they share them equally with all sentient beings and dedicate them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Subhūti, you should know that the merit resulting from such a bodhisattva’s rejoicing and dedication of all meritorious deeds surpasses by a hundredfold, a thousandfold, and even up to an *upaniṣad*-fold the merit of all those previously mentioned bodhisattvas who practice meritorious deeds through the conjunction of prajñā and other roots of goodness, employing the method of apprehending something as real.

Why is this? Because those bodhisattvas perform various meritorious deeds together with their prajñā and other roots of goodness by means of apprehending something; whereas these bodhisattvas’ sympathetic joy and dedication are performed by means of non-apprehension.
Chapter Seven: The Hells, Part Four of the Fourth Division. At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
You should know that the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is itself the nature of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), and it is perfectly capable of accomplishing the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*).”
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śāriputra, saying: "So it is! So it is!"
"It is as you have said.
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:

“The profound *prajñāpāramitā* is able to provide illumination and should be honored by all; it cannot be defiled by any worldly phenomena. It can dispel the darkness and obscurations and bring forth radiant light; it bestows benefit and peace, ever acting as the foremost leader. It serves as pure eyes for the blind and as a bright lamp for those traveling through the dark. It leads those who have lost their way into the correct path and reveals the nature of all phenomena as omniscience (*sarvajñatā*). It demonstrates that all phenomena are neither extinguished nor born. It is the mother of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, providing refuge and protection for those without refuge or protection. It can eliminate all the sufferings and afflictions of birth and death, and reveal that the nature of all phenomena is the absence of intrinsic nature. It enables all Buddhas to fully turn the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma with its three revolutions and twelve aspects.”
“World-Honored One!
How should the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in this profound prajñāpāramitā?
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śāriputra, saying:

“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should dwell in profound prajñāpāramitā as they would dwell in the presence of the Buddha; they should contemplate and honor profound prajñāpāramitā as they would contemplate and honor the Buddha.”
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, thought to himself:
"For what cause and for what reason does Śāriputra now ask the Buddha about this matter?
Having reflected thus, he asked Śāriputra:
“For what reason do you ask this?
At that time, Śāriputra said to Śakra:

“The former Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, have taught that because they are embraced by the skillful means of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas are able to swiftly realize the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) through the meritorious deeds associated with sympathetic joy and dedication. This is superior to the generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, wisdom, and other roots of virtue of those bodhisattvas who perceive things as having objective existence.”
For this reason, I ask about this matter. "Kauśika!

Suppose there were a multitude of those born blind, numbering a hundred or a thousand, who lacked a guide with pure vision to lead them by skillful means; they would not even be able to enter the right path when it was near, let alone reach the great city of abundance and joy from afar!"

In this way, these groups of those born blind—the first five perfections—cannot even set out upon the correct path of a bodhisattva if they lack the guidance of the pure eye of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), much less can they enter the city of omniscience (sarvajñatā)!
Kauśika! The five pāramitās, beginning with generosity, must rely upon the prajñāpāramitā to be designated as "possessing eyes.
Furthermore, it is through being embraced by the prajñāpāramitā that they are designated as "reaching the other shore" (pāramitā).
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva bring forth the perfection of wisdom?
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
“Śāriputra, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas bring forth the perfection of wisdom just as they bring forth form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.”
Just as the five aggregates of clinging are not to be brought forth, so too should the profound *prajñāpāramitā* be understood.

Śāriputra, just as the five aggregates of clinging are said to be "brought forth" because they are not brought forth, so too is the profound *prajñāpāramitā*; it is said to be "brought forth" because it is not brought forth.
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“By thus eliciting the profound perfection of wisdom, for the accomplishment of what dharma do the bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice?”
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

“When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas thus bring forth this profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they accomplish nothing at all regarding any phenomena. Because they accomplish nothing regarding any phenomena, it is called the perfection of wisdom.”
Then Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Can the profound *prajñāpāramitā* not bring about the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*)?
At that time, the Buddha said to Śakra, Lord of the Devas:
"So it is! So it is! It is just as you have said."
Even the profound *prajñāpāramitā* cannot bring about the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*).
Why is this? Kauśika!
"Because that which is attained cannot be established; because that which is named and conceptualized cannot be established; because that which is produced and constructed cannot be established.
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"How does the profound Prajñāpāramitā explain the accomplishment of the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)?"
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of Devas, saying:
"Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* does not establish anything regarding the omniscience it brings forth, it is said to be 'established'."
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“How extraordinary!
World-Honored One!”
"How marvelous, O Sugata!

This profound *prajñāpāramitā* appears in the world not for the sake of the arising and ceasing of all phenomena, nor for the sake of the formation and disintegration of all phenomena, yet it brings great benefit to the world."
At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought as this:”
"If the profound *prajñāpāramitā* [is concerned with] the arising or ceasing, or the formation or disintegration,
of all phenomena," that bodhisattva mahāsattva will then abandon and distance themselves from the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.
The Buddha told Subhūti: “So it is! So it is!”
Furthermore, there is another cause and condition by which bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abandon and distance themselves from this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, namely, giving rise to this thought:
"The profound *prajñāpāramitā* is non-existent, not real, not solid, and not independent."
This bodhisattva-mahāsattva will then abandon and distance himself from the profound *prajñāpāramitā*. Why is this?

Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is neither existent nor non-existent, neither false nor real, neither solid nor insubstantial, and neither autonomous nor non-autonomous, for it is without conceptual differentiation regarding all phenomena.
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“By what dharma does the Buddha intend to reveal when he speaks of this profound *prajñāpāramitā*?
The Buddha told Subhūti:
“I say that this profound *prajñāpāramitā* reveals nothing at all. Why is this?

Within this profound teaching of the *prajñāpāramitā*, form (*rūpa*) is not revealed, nor are feeling (*vedanā*), perception (*saṃjñā*), formations (*saṃskāra*), or consciousness (*vijñāna*) revealed; the fruit of stream-entry (*srotāpattiphala*) is not revealed, nor are the fruits of once-returning (*sakṛdāgāmiphala*), non-returning (*anāgāmiphala*), arhatship (*arhattvaphala*), or the enlightenment of a solitary buddha (*pratyekabuddhabodhi*) revealed; nor are the practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas or the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all buddhas (*anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi*) revealed.”
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"The profound perfection of wisdom is itself the vast perfection.
The Buddha told Subhūti:
“Based on what intention do you say this:
‘The profound perfection of wisdom is itself the vast perfection of wisdom’?
Subhūti replied:

"The profound perfection of wisdom does not make form great, nor does it make it small; it likewise does not make feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness great, nor does it make them small.
It does not make form accumulate, nor does it make it disperse; it likewise does not make feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness accumulate, nor does it make them disperse.
It does not make form powerful, nor does it make it powerless; it likewise does not make feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness powerful, nor does it make them powerless."

In this way, up to and including the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, one does not conceive of them as great or small; nor does one conceive of the omniscient wisdom (sarvajñajñāna) attained by those Buddhas as great or small.
One does not conceive of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas as gathered or dispersed; nor does one conceive of the omniscient wisdom attained by those Buddhas as gathered or dispersed.
One does not conceive of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas as powerful or powerless; nor does one conceive of the omniscient wisdom attained by those Buddhas as powerful or powerless.

Why is this? Because the five aggregates, up to and including the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), are neither great nor small, neither accumulated nor dispersed, and neither powerful nor powerless, for the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is empty.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such conceptions, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
Why is this? Because such conceptions are not the natural outflow (niṣyanda-phala) of the profound perfection of wisdom.
"The profound perfection of wisdom does not have such a thought as:
'I shall deliver so many sentient beings and cause them to enter the realm of nirvana without remainder.'"
If one possesses such a conception, it is then called "great.
There is that which is attained and that which is not attained, yet it is capable of accomplishing what must be done. Why is this so?
Because sentient beings are unborn, one should know that the perfection of wisdom is also unborn;
because sentient beings lack intrinsic nature, one should know that the perfection of wisdom also lacks intrinsic nature;
because sentient beings are detached, one should know that the perfection of wisdom is also detached.
Because sentient beings are inconceivable, one should know that the perfection of wisdom is also inconceivable;
because sentient beings are not subject to destruction, one should know that the perfection of wisdom is also not subject to destruction;
because sentient beings lack cognitive awareness, one should know that the perfection of wisdom also lacks cognitive awareness.
Because sentient beings do not realize the reality of suchness, one should know that the perfection of wisdom also does not realize the reality of suchness;
because the power of sentient beings is not accomplished, one should know that the power of the perfection of wisdom is also not accomplished.
“World-Honored One!
It is for this reason that I say:
the profound perfection of wisdom is itself the vast perfection of wisdom.”
"Why is this? Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* accomplishes great tasks.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to have profound faith and understanding in this deep prajñāpāramitā, being without doubt, without confusion, and without delusion, from where did that bodhisattva mahāsattva pass away to come and be born in this realm?”
"For how long has this Bodhisattva Mahāsattva practiced the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, such that he is able to realize and understand its profound meaning?
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

"This Bodhisattva Mahāsattva has passed away from the assemblies of Buddhas whom he served throughout the worlds of the ten directions and has been reborn here. This Bodhisattva Mahāsattva has already practiced the profound *prajñāpāramitā* for immeasurable and incalculable great eons (*mahākalpa*), and is thus able to realize and understand its profound meaning."

Why is this? If a bodhisattva mahāsattva has passed away from the assemblies of various Buddhas in other world-systems where they served them and has come to be born here, that bodhisattva mahāsattva has already extensively attended upon the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and has previously inquired about the profound meanings of the Dharma herein. Upon seeing or hearing this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they will think:
"I am now seeing the Buddha and hearing what the Buddha has spoken."

By virtue of these causes and conditions, if one hears the profound *prajñāpāramitā* being proclaimed, one listens with focused attention, reverently accepts it with faith, and severs all doubts regarding its profound meaning and principles.

Śāriputra! This bodhisattva mahāsattva has already made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas and has practiced the profound perfection of wisdom for many kalpas; therefore, in this present life, he is able to accomplish such a task.
At that time, Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:

"Can this profound *prajñāpāramitā* be heard? Can it be observed? Can it be brought forth? Can it be recollected? Can it be manifested as 'this' or 'that'? Can the distinctions of place and time be made clear? Can its various modes, characteristics, and signs be proclaimed so as to reveal the profound meaning of the *prajñāpāramitā*?"
The Buddha said:
"No, Subhūti! You should know this!"
The profound *prajñāpāramitā* cannot be demonstrated through the specific natures of the aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), or sense-bases (*āyatana*). Why is this?
Because all phenomena are ultimately secluded; it is impossible to demonstrate the profound *prajñāpāramitā* by means of phenomena that are not themselves secluded.
Subhūti, you should know that the profound perfection of wisdom is detached from the aggregates, elements, and sense bases,
and thus cannot be realized. Why is this?

The very aggregates, elements, and sense bases that realize all phenomena to be ultimately detached are called the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā); therefore, the perfection of wisdom is non-dual and inseparable from the aggregates, elements, and sense bases.

Subhūti, you should know that because all phenomena are ultimately empty, their nature is detached, and they are eternally quiescent, they are unapprehendable; this very unapprehensibility is what is called the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
Subhūti, you should know that when there is neither perception nor the designation of equal perception through verbal expression, at that time it is called the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“For how long must Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas accumulate their practice before they are able to diligently study and cultivate the profound perfection of wisdom?”
The Buddha told Subhūti:
"This should be distinguished, for the faculties of bodhisattvas differ.
