Subhūti, you should know this!"

There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, from the moment they first resolve their minds [on awakening], encounter true spiritual friends who skillfully guide and sustain them, enabling them to practice and study the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.

Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess skillful means, they do not slander the true Dharma; they do not perceive any increase or decrease among all phenomena; they never depart from the correct practice of a bodhisattva; they never distance themselves from the Buddhas and bodhisattvas; they constantly plant roots of goodness with pure body and mind; they adorn and purify buddha-fields and bring sentient beings to maturity, thereby swiftly attaining the knowledge of all modes.

“There are sons of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who, although they have previously seen many hundreds of thousands of buddhas and have practiced the holy life in the presence of those buddhas, are unable to study the profound *prajñāpāramitā* because they employ the method of grasping at attainments. Upon hearing this profound *prajñāpāramitā* being taught, they do not give rise to faith or understanding, and they immediately depart.”

Why is this? Because these sons of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle, in the presence of past Buddhas, did not hear the profound *prajñāpāramitā* being proclaimed with reverence; because they lacked reverence, they did not listen to it frequently; because they did not listen to it frequently, they were unable to draw near to it; because they could not draw near to it, they were unable to inquire about it; because they did not inquire about it, they were unable to believe and understand it; and because they lacked belief and understanding, they abandoned the assembly and departed.

Due to these causes and conditions, they have created and increased karma that obstructs the True Dharma; by the power of past habituation, when they now hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā* being taught, they depart once again, failing to give rise to reverence and being unable to accept it with faith. Because they do not accept it with faith, their bodies and minds are neither in harmony; because they are not in harmony, they are unable to comprehend the profound meaning and intent of this *prajñāpāramitā*.

They are unable to believe in, hear, understand, or contemplate the profound meaning and intent of the *prajñāpāramitā*. They create and increase karma that impoverishes the True Dharma; by virtue of this karma, they create and increase the sinful karma of impaired wisdom, and by virtue of this karma, upon hearing the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they slander, revile, and abandon it.

"Subhūti, you should know that those sons of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who revile, detest, and abandon this profound *prajñāpāramitā* are, in fact, reviling, detesting, and abandoning the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvajñājñāna*) of all Buddhas of the three times."

Due to these causes and conditions, they commit and increase extremely heavy evil karma; because of this karma, they fall into the great hells and undergo various intense sufferings for a long period of time. Because their past habitual heavy evil karma has caused their awakening-wisdom and roots of goodness to become entirely feeble, and because their merit is meager, they harm themselves and others. Although they have developed a small degree of faith, acceptance, and aspiration toward the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, due to their ignorance, they are unable to discern the depth or shallowness of the true Dharma.
They themselves slander and reject the Mahāyāna, and they also cause newly initiated sentient beings who uphold the true Dharma to slander and reject the Mahāyāna teachings, saying:
"The profound *prajñāpāramitā* is not the true word of the Buddha; it should not be studied."
Since they cause others to slander the *prajñāpāramitā*, they themselves also deeply slander the *prajñāpāramitā*.
Since they have thus slandered the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they also deeply slander *sarvajñatā*.
Due to their profound slander of the power of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), they also profoundly slander the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha; by this, they commit extremely heavy evil karma.

Through the causal conditions of the growth of this evil karma, they fall into the great hells and undergo various intense sufferings, remaining there for many hundreds of thousands of years without attaining liberation.
"Because his offenses are grave, he shall pass from one great hell to another within this world, undergoing various intense sufferings until the kalpas of fire, water, and wind have not yet arisen."

If, in this world, any of the calamities of fire, water, or wind should arise during a kalpa of destruction, because their heavy and evil karma is not yet exhausted, they die and are reborn in a similar great hell in another world, where they undergo various intense sufferings for many hundreds of thousands of years.

Because their offenses are so grave, they shall pass from one great hell to another in other world-systems, undergoing various intense sufferings until the kalpas of fire, water, and wind have not yet arisen.

If a kalpa-ending fire, water, or wind arises in another world-system, because their heavy and evil karma is not yet exhausted, they die and are reborn in a similar great hell in another world-system, where they undergo various intense sufferings for many hundreds of thousands of years.

Because their offenses are so grave, they travel from one great hell to another within other world-systems, undergoing various intense sufferings until the kalpas of fire, water, and wind have not yet arisen; thus, they pass through them in succession, experiencing various intense sufferings throughout the great hells of the ten directions.

When the fire, water, and wind kalpas arise in those other worlds of the ten directions, because their heavy and evil karma has not yet been exhausted, they die and are reborn again within the great hells of this Sahā world; from one great hell to another great hell, they undergo various intense sufferings until the fire, water, and wind kalpas have arisen.

If any of the kalpas of fire, water, or wind should arise in this world, because their heavy and evil karma is not yet exhausted, they die and are reborn again in other worlds throughout the ten directions, experiencing various intense sufferings within the great hells.

"Thus they wander in saṃsāra for incalculable kalpas; when the force of that karma of slandering the Dharma has somewhat diminished, they emerge from hell and fall into the realm of animals, where they continue to cycle through various states in their own world and other regions, undergoing manifold sufferings for many kalpas."

The force of their karma from slandering the Dharma has somewhat diminished; thus they avoid rebirth in the animal realm and instead fall into the realm of hungry ghosts, where they wander through this world and other realms, undergoing various sufferings for incalculable eons.

As the residual force of that karma of slandering the Dharma was about to be exhausted, he departed from the realm of hungry ghosts and was reborn among humans. Although he attained human form, he dwelt in a lowly and base station; he was blind, deaf, mute, frequently ill, impoverished, ugly, and dull-witted. All people looked down upon and ridiculed him; wherever he was born, there was little joy and much suffering, and he never heard the names of the Buddha, the Dharma, or the Sangha.
"Why is this? Because he slandered the Triple Gem through the evil karma of his speech, he must undergo such a complete fruit of suffering.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Are the offense of slandering the Dharma and the karma of the immediate retribution similar to one another?
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śāriputra, saying:
"Do not say that this offense is like the karma of the five deeds of immediate retribution. Why is this?

Although the five deeds of immediate retribution result in heavy suffering, they cannot be compared to the slandering of the True Dharma; for instance, when one hears the teaching of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, one slanders and rejects it, saying: "

"To say, 'This Prajñāpāramitā is not the true word of the Buddha; it should not be studied, for it is not the Dharma, not the Vinaya, and not the teaching of the Great Master'—by reason of this cause and condition, one's transgression is extremely grave."

“Śāriputra! These people who slander the Dharma slander the True Dharma themselves and incite others to slander it; they destroy their own bodies and cause others to destroy theirs; they drink poison themselves and make others drink it; they lose for themselves the blissful fruits of rebirth in heaven and liberation and cause others to lose them as well; they consign their own bodies to the fires of hell and cause others to do so; and while they themselves lack faith and understanding in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they teach others not to have faith or understanding, leading them into delusion and inversion so that they sink into the sea of suffering and drown others as well.”
Śāriputra! Regarding this profound Prajñāpāramitā, I do not even wish for those who would slander the True Dharma to hear its name, much less for me to explain it to them!
Śāriputra! I do not even permit those sons of good family who have set out in the bodhisattva vehicle to hear the name of one who slanders the true Dharma, let alone see them with their own eyes!
"How could I permit them to dwell together? Śāriputra!
As for those who slander the True Dharma, I do not even allow them to wear the kāṣāya; how much less could they receive offerings!"
Why is this? Śāriputra!

You should know that all those who revile the profound *prajñāpāramitā* are destroyers of the True Dharma; they belong to the class of darkness like foul snails, defiling themselves and others like a heap of putrid excrement.
"Those who place their trust in the words of such destroyers of the Dharma shall likewise undergo the great sufferings as previously described.
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"For what reason does the Tathāgata not describe the physical appearance and the dimensions of the bodies of those who destroy the true Dharma, and the miserable realms into which they shall fall?"
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
"Cease! You should not speak of the physical appearance or bodily dimensions that those who destroy the True Dharma will receive in the future."

Why is this? If I were to describe in detail the dimensions and forms of those realms, those who hear it would be struck with terror and vomit hot blood, leading to their death or the suffering of near-death; their minds would suddenly be afflicted by grief as if pierced by a poisoned arrow, and their bodies would gradually wither away like cut-down stalks.

I fear that upon hearing it said that those who slander the True Dharma shall receive such a body of great and loathsome suffering, they would in vain become terrified and lose their lives; out of compassion for them, I do not speak it for you.

Then, Śāriputra requested the Tathāgata for a second and a third time that he describe the dimensions of those [retributions], clearly admonishing future generations so that they might know how slandering the Dharma results in a body of great suffering and refrain from committing such a transgression.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śāriputra, saying:
"What I have previously stated regarding the suffering of the evil realms incurred by the sin of destroying the True Dharma is sufficient as a clear warning.

When those of our own kind, such as good sons and others, hear what I have said before concerning the retribution for slandering the Dharma, they would rather sacrifice their bodies and lives than ever slander the Dharma, lest they themselves suffer such misery in the future."
At that time, Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:

“Any intelligent sons of good family who hear the Buddha’s teaching regarding how those who slander the Dharma will endure great suffering for a long time in future worlds, should carefully guard the actions of their body, speech, and mind.”
Why is this? Lest, because of these evil words, I should suffer for a long time among those in the evil destinies and the human realm.
World-Honored One!
“Is it not because of practicing various evil deeds that one creates and increases karma that destroys the True Dharma?
The Buddha told Subhūti: “It is so!”

"It is so! Within my true Dharma and Vinaya, there will be certain foolish renunciants who, though they claim me as their Great Teacher, will slander and reject the profound Prajñāpāramitā that I have taught."
Subhūti, you should know this:
if one slanders the profound *prajñā*, one slanders unsurpassed enlightenment.
If one slanders unsurpassed enlightenment, one slanders the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*).
If one slanders the knowledge of all modes, one thereby slanders the Triple Gem of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha.
If one slanders the Triple Gem of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha, one then incurs boundless karmic offenses.
"If one takes up boundless sinful karma, then one will take up boundless retribution of suffering.
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"By how many causes and conditions do those foolish people slander such profound *prajñāpāramitā*?"
The Buddha told Subhūti:
“It is by way of four causes and conditions. What are these four?”
First, because they are incited and deluded by various evil māras and demons;
second, because they lack faith and understanding toward the profound Dharma;
and third, because they do not apply themselves with diligence but instead become attached to the five aggregates and are taken under the influence of evil associates.
Fourth, they harbor much malice, delight in practicing unwholesome dharmas, and take pleasure in self-exaltation while disparaging others.
Because those foolish people possess these four causes and conditions, they slander the *prajñāpāramitā*, and by virtue of this, they shall undergo various intense sufferings in the future.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 544; The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra,
Fascicle 545.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
Chapter 8: On Purity, Part Four. Chapter Eight: On Purity. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”

Those who are foolish and lack diligent effort, who are possessed of various evil deeds and meager roots of virtue, who are dull-witted, lacking in aspiration, of little learning, and of inferior wisdom; who are taken in by evil associates and do not serve virtuous friends; who take no pleasure in inquiring about supreme virtues and do not apply themselves to study—such people find it truly difficult to believe in and understand the profound *prajñāpāramitā* spoken by the Buddha.
The Buddha told Subhūti: “So it is! So it is!”
"It is as you have said.
At that time, Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"In this way, why is the Prajñāpāramitā so profound, difficult to believe, and difficult to understand?"
The Buddha told Subhūti:
"Form is neither bound nor liberated. Why is this?"
Because form has non-existence as its intrinsic nature,
feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated. Why is this?
Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness have non-existence as their intrinsic nature.
"Furthermore, Subhūti,
the prior limit of form is neither bound nor liberated."
Why is this? Because the prior limit of form has non-existence as its intrinsic nature;
thus, the posterior limit of form is neither bound nor liberated.
Why is this? Because the future limit of form has the absence of intrinsic nature as its own nature;
within the middle limit of form, there is neither bondage nor liberation.
Why is this? Because the middle limit of form has the absence of intrinsic nature as its own nature.
Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated at their prior limit.
Why is this? Because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness have non-existence as their intrinsic nature regarding their prior limit.
Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated regarding their posterior limit.
Why is this? Because the future limit of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness has the absence of intrinsic nature as its own nature.
Within feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, there is neither bondage nor liberation.
"Why is this? Because the middle limit of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness has the absence of intrinsic nature as its own nature.
The Venerable Subhūti then addressed the Buddha again, saying:
“The profound perfection of wisdom is extremely difficult to believe and understand!
The profound perfection of wisdom is exceedingly difficult to believe and understand!
The Buddha said to Subhūti:
"So it is! So it is! It is just as you have said."
Why is that? Subhūti!
The purity of form is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of form.
Why is this? Because this purity of form and the purity of the fruit are non-dual, not divided into two, distinct, or separate.

The purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is itself the purity of the fruit; the purity of the fruit is itself the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.

Why is this? Because this purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is non-dual with the purity of the fruit; it is not divided into two, it is not distinct, and it is not discontinuous.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
The purity of form is the purity of all-knowledge; the purity of all-knowledge is the purity of form. Why is this?
This purity of form and the purity of omniscience are non-dual; they are not two, not distinct, and not separate.

The purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is itself the purity of omniscience, and the purity of omniscience is itself the purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.

Why is this? Because this purity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness is non-dual with the purity of all-knowledge; it is not divided into two, it is not distinct, and there is no separation between them.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is most profound.”
The Buddha said, “It is so!
Because it is utterly pure.”
Śāriputra said, “In this way,
the Prajñāpāramitā is truly capable of illuminating and comprehending.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because it is utterly pure. Śāriputra said:
“In this way, the perfection of wisdom is a great illumination.
The Buddha said, “So it is!”
“Because it is utterly pure. Śāriputra said:
“In this way, the perfection of wisdom never continues on.”
The Buddha said: “It is so!
Because it is utterly pure.”
Śāriputra said:
"In this way, the Prajñāpāramitā is fundamentally free from defilement.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because it is utterly pure. Śāriputra said:
"In this way, the perfection of wisdom is without attainment and without clear realization.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
"Because it is utterly pure. Śāriputra said:
"In this way, the Prajñāpāramitā is without arising."
The Buddha said: "It is so!
Because it is utterly pure."
Śāriputra said:
“In this way, the perfection of wisdom is ultimately non-arising.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because it is utterly pure. Śāriputra said:
"In this way, the perfection of wisdom is not produced in the desire realm, not produced in the form realm, and not produced in the formless realm.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
"Because it is utterly pure. Śāriputra said:
"In this way, the Prajñāpāramitā is without cognition and without understanding."
The Buddha said: "It is so!
Because it is utterly pure."
Śāriputra said:
“In what phenomena does this prajñāpāramitā have no knowledge and no understanding?
The Buddha said:
"There is no knowledge and no understanding regarding form. Why is this?
Because it is utterly pure."
There is no knowledge and no understanding regarding feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness. Why is this?
Because they are utterly pure.
Śāriputra said:
"In this way, the perfection of wisdom neither diminishes nor augments omniscience (sarvajñatā).
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because it is utterly pure. Śāriputra said:
"In this way, the perfection of wisdom neither grasps nor abandons any phenomena.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
"Because it is utterly pure.
At that time, Subhūti also addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Because I am pure, form is pure."
The Buddha said: “So it is!
Because it is ultimately pure.”
Subhūti spoke again:
"Because I am pure, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are pure.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because it is ultimately pure.
Subhūti spoke again:
“Because I am pure, the fruit is pure.
The Buddha said, “So it is!”
"Because it is ultimately pure.
Subhūti spoke again:
"Because I am pure, all-knowledge is pure."
The Buddha said: “It is so!
Because it is ultimately pure.”
Subhūti spoke again:
“Because I am pure, there is neither attainment nor clear realization.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because it is ultimately pure.
Subhūti spoke again:
"Because I am infinite, form is infinite.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
“Because it is ultimately pure.
Subhūti spoke again:
“Because the self is limitless, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are limitless.”
The Buddha said: “It is so!
Because it is ultimately pure.”
Subhūti spoke again:
"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can awaken in this way, this is the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because it is ultimately pure.
Subhūti spoke again:
"In this way, the perfection of wisdom is neither this shore, nor the other shore, nor does it abide in between.
The Buddha said, "So it is!"
"Because it is ultimately pure.
Subhūti spoke again:
"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to such a conceptualization, they abandon the perfection of wisdom and distance themselves from the perfection of wisdom."
The Buddha told Subhūti: “So it is! So it is!”
"Why is this? It is because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are attached to names and attached to signs.
The Venerable Subhūti then addressed the Buddha, saying:
"How extraordinary!
World-Honored One!
How rare!"
Well-spoken, Sugata!
You have well explained, for the sake of the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, the ultimate attachment to signs within the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.
At that time, Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"In what way does a bodhisattva mahāsattva give rise to the mark of attachment toward the profound perfection of wisdom?"
Subhūti replied:

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva conceives the notion of emptiness regarding form as being empty, conceives the notion of emptiness regarding feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness as being empty; if they conceive the notion of past phenomena regarding past phenomena, the notion of future phenomena regarding future phenomena, and the notion of present phenomena regarding present phenomena—then even if such sons of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva Vehicle have generated merit at the time of their initial resolve, they are nevertheless said to be attached to signs."
Then Śakra, Lord of the Devas, asked Subhūti:
"For what reason is this called 'clinging to signs'?
Subhūti replied:

"If one thinks, 'This is the Great Bodhicitta,' or if one clings to this as being the initial Bodhicitta while dedicating it toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, this is called 'clinging to signs.'"
Kauśika! The intrinsic nature of the mind is empty and cannot be dedicated.
If sons of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle should form such an attachment:
"I am one who has entered the Great Vehicle"—
all such [statements] are termed "clinging to signs.

Therefore, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas wish to manifest, exhort, encourage, and gladden sentient beings so that they may set out upon the Great Vehicle for the sake of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they should manifest, exhort, encourage, and gladden them in accordance with the true nature of reality (*dharmatā*).

If those sentient beings can thus manifest such demonstrations, provide such exhortations, offer such encouragement, and bestow such joy upon other sentient beings, they will neither harm themselves nor harm others; this is what all Tathāgatas would approve of.

Kauśika! If sons of good family who abide in the Mahāyāna can thus demonstrate, exhort, encourage, and gladden sentient beings who are approaching the Bodhisattva vehicle, they will be able to remain far removed from all attachments.
At that time, the World-Honored One praised Subhūti, saying:
“Excellent! Excellent!”
"You have now skillfully explained the characteristics of attachment for the sake of all bodhisattvas, enabling them to recognize and distance themselves from it.
Furthermore, there are other subtle attachments that I shall explain to you; you should listen attentively!"
"Excellent is your attention.
Subhūti replied, "So be it!"
“Please speak!
We wish to hear it.
The Buddha told Subhūti:

“Sons of good family who dwell securely in the Mahāyāna and wish to proceed toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, if they take up signs and bring them to mind with pure faith regarding the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, whatever signs they thus take up are all termed attachments.”
Why is this so? Because those who grasp at signs are said to be attached.

If one deeply rejoices in all the untainted dharmas of the past, future, and present Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and furthermore takes these roots of goodness born of such rejoicing and, together with all sentient beings, dedicates them equally toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, this too is called attachment.
Why is this so? Because the true nature of all phenomena is neither past, nor future, nor present; it is remote from the three periods of time.

It is not possible to dedicate [merit] by means of that which is remote from the three periods of time, because phenomena remote from the three periods of time cannot be grasped as signs, cannot be taken as objects of perception, and are devoid of the activities of seeing, hearing, sensing, or knowing.
The Venerable Subhūti then addressed the Buddha, saying,
"The true nature of all phenomena is most profound.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because its intrinsic nature is detached.
Subhūti spoke again:
"In this way, the intrinsic nature of the perfection of wisdom is profoundly deep.
The Buddha said, "It is so!"
"Because its intrinsic nature is pure.
Subhūti spoke again:
"In this way, the intrinsic nature of the perfection of wisdom is pure."
The Buddha said,
"It is so! Because its intrinsic nature is detached."
Subhūti spoke again:
“In this way, one should pay homage to the perfection of wisdom.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! Because all phenomena are by nature detached.
Subhūti, you should know this!"
If all phenomena are by nature remote and detached, that is precisely the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*). Why is this?
Because the Tathāgata has realized and awakened to the true nature of all phenomena as being without fabrication and without action.

if they do not abide in feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, nor abide in the thought ‘this is feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness,’ this is training in feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.”

Furthermore, Kauśika, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), if they do not train in form (rūpa), nor train in the thought "this is form," they do not abide in form;

if they do not train in feeling (vedanā), perception (saṃjñā), formations (saṃskāra), or consciousness (vijñāna), nor train in the thought "this is feeling, perception, formation, or consciousness," they do not abide in feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness.

Kauśika! This is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the profound perfection of wisdom; it is also called abiding in the profound perfection of wisdom; and it is also called training in the profound perfection of wisdom.
Then, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:

“In this way, the Prajñāpāramitā is most profound; in this way, the Prajñāpāramitā is difficult to fathom; in this way, the Prajñāpāramitā is difficult to grasp; in this way, the Prajñāpāramitā is without limit.”
At that time, the Buddha said to Śāriputra: "So it is! So it is!"

Śāriputra! When bodhisattva mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom, if they do not abide in the profundity of form, nor abide in the thought that "this is the profundity of form," this is called training in the profundity of form;

if they do not abide in the profundity of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, nor abide in the thought that "this is the profundity of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness," this is called training in the profundity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the profound perfection of wisdom, if they do not train in the profundity of form, nor train in the thought that "this is the profundity of form," this is called non-abiding in the profundity of form.

If they do not train in the profundity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, nor train in the thought that "this is the profundity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness," this is called non-abiding in the profundity of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:

"Since this Prajñāpāramitā is thus most profound, difficult to fathom, difficult to grasp, and without limit, it is difficult to believe and understand; it should be taught only to those bodhisattvas who are at the stage of non-retrogression."

Why is this? Because upon hearing such profound *prajñāpāramitā*, their minds are not startled, terrified, or filled with doubt; they do not give rise to slander, but instead possess deep-seated faith and understanding.
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, asked the Venerable Śāriputra:
"If one were to teach this profound perfection of wisdom to those bodhisattvas who have not yet received their prediction [of enlightenment], what fault would there be?"
Then, Śāriputra said to Śakra:

“Upon hearing this, they will be startled, terrified, and filled with doubt; they will be unable to believe or understand it, and may even give rise to slander. Because of this, they will create and increase karma that leads to rebirth in the evil destinies, sinking into the three miserable realms to undergo great suffering for a long time, making it difficult for them to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
"Therefore, one should not proclaim this profound *prajñāpāramitā* to them.
Śakra, Lord of Devas, said:

"Is it possible that there might be a bodhisattva who, though not yet having received a prediction of enlightenment, upon hearing this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, does not become startled, terrified, or doubtful, and does not give rise to slander, but instead possesses deep faith and understanding?"
Śāriputra said: "There is, Kauśika!"

This bodhisattva mahāsattva has long since resolved upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment; he has long cultivated the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and it will not be long before he receives the prophecy of great bodhi.

Kauśika! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, is not startled, terrified, or filled with doubt, and does not give rise to slander but instead possesses deep faith and understanding, you should know that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has already received the prediction of unexcelled great enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*). Even if they have not yet received it, they will certainly receive the prediction of great enlightenment at the hands of no more than one or two Buddhas.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śāriputra, saying: “So it is! So it is!”
It is as you have said, Śāriputra!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva has long studied the Mahāyāna, long made great vows, and long cultivated the great practices; if they have made offerings to many Buddhas, served many virtuous friends, and their roots of goodness are matured; then upon hearing this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, their mind will not be startled, terrified, or filled with doubt. With deep faith and understanding, they will always delight in hearing, receiving, upholding, reading, and reciting it; they will respectfully make offerings to it, contemplate it according to the principle, explain it to others, or transcribe it, practicing as taught without ever becoming weary.

Śāriputra! By virtue of these causes and conditions, wherever this bodhisattva mahāsattva is born, he constantly beholds the Buddhas and perpetually hears the True Dharma; he makes offerings, pays homage, respects, and praises them.
Whichever Buddha he encounters, he receives a prediction of enlightenment from that Buddha, and none of his encounters pass in vain.
Then, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“I now wish to offer a brief analogy; I only pray that you will grant me leave to speak.
At that time, the Buddha said to Śāriputra:
"Speak as you wish.
Then, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

If sons of good family who abide in the Mahāyāna dream that they themselves are seated upon the sublime seat of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), one should know that such persons are close to realizing unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

In this way, if there are sons of good family or others who, upon hearing the *prajñāpāramitā*, develop deep faith and reverence, and then receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect according to principle, copy, explain, and cause it to be widely disseminated, one should know that these persons have long studied the Mahāyāna and their roots of goodness are matured; they have either already received the prediction of great enlightenment (*mahābodhi*), or are close to receiving the prediction of great enlightenment, and will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*).
“World-Honored One!

It is as if there were a person traveling through a vast wilderness, passing through dangerous paths of one hundred, or two, or three, or four, or five hundred *yojanas*, who sees the preliminary signs of a city or royal capital—such as herdsmen, groves, and fields—and having seen these signs, he thinks:
‘The city or royal capital is not far from here.’”
Having formed this thought, his body and mind became serene; he feared neither wild beasts, nor evil bandits, nor hunger and thirst.

It is the same for sons of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle: if they hear the *prajñāpāramitā* and, with deep resolve, believe and revere it, receiving, upholding, reciting, diligently practicing, reflecting according to the principle, copying, explaining, and widely disseminating it—then one should know that such persons will before long receive the prediction (*vyākaraṇa*) of great enlightenment, swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*), and have no fear of falling into the stages of the Śrāvaka or Pratyekabuddha.
Why is this? Because they have already obtained the prior signs of seeing, hearing, making offerings to, and revering the unsurpassed enlightenment of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.
“World-Honored One! [he said.]
For example, suppose there is a person who wishes to behold the great ocean; traveling toward it gradually over a long period of time, when they see no mountains or forests, they think to themselves:
"Judging by these signs now, the great ocean is not far away."
"Why is this? Because near the great ocean, the ground must gradually descend and be devoid of mountains and forests.
At that time, although that person had not yet seen the sea, seeing these proximate signs, he was filled with joy and leaped for gladness.

It is the same for sons of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle: if they hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā* and give rise to deep faith and reverence, receiving, upholding, reading, reciting, diligently practicing, reflecting according to the principle, transcribing, explaining, and widely disseminating it, one should know that such persons will before long receive the prediction of great enlightenment and swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.
Why is this? Because they have already heard this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, which is the precursor to unsurpassed enlightenment.
"World-Honored One!"
For example, in the springtime, when the flowers and fruits of trees have already shed their old leaves and their branches and twigs are lush and moist, all who see them think:
"It will not be long before new flowers, fruits, and leaves emerge."
Why is this? Because these trees have first manifested the signs of new flowers, fruits, and leaves.

In the same way, sons of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle, if they hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā* and, with deep faith and reverence, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to the principle, copy, explain, and cause it to be widely disseminated;
"You should know that this person will before long receive the prophecy of great enlightenment and swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.

World-Honored One! It is like a woman who has been pregnant for some time; her body grows increasingly heavy and her movements become unsteady. Her appetite for food and drink, as well as her sleep, all diminish. She takes no pleasure in much speech and grows weary of her usual activities. Because she suffers from pain, all her tasks suddenly cease. When another woman observes these signs, she immediately knows that this woman will give birth before long."

It is likewise for sons of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle: if they hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā* and, with deep faith and reverence, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to the principle, transcribe, explain, and cause it to be widely disseminated, you should know that such persons will before long receive the prophecy of great enlightenment, swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, and turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver the multitudes of sentient beings.
At that time, the Buddha praised Śāriputra, saying:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
"You have skillfully explained the parables of the bodhisattvas;
you should know that these are all due to the spiritual power of the Tathāgata.
*The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Scroll 545 (part 2), Scroll 544.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang under Imperial Order.
Part Four, Chapter Ten on Dhāraṇī, Section Two. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
It is rare indeed that the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha so skillfully analyzes and explains the matters concerning all bodhisattvas.
The Buddha told Subhūti:
"So it is! So it is! Why is this so?

The bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, desiring to bring benefit and happiness to many sentient beings, out of compassion for the great multitude of beings in the world, and out of pity for humans and devas so that they may attain great purpose, benefit, and happiness, seek to realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening and preach the unsurpassed Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings.
At that time, Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“All bodhisattva mahāsattvas have accomplished an infinite mass of great merit; for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, they practice the profound perfection of wisdom.”
“How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva practice the perfection of wisdom so as to swiftly attain its fulfillment?
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they do not perceive an increase in form while practicing the perfection of wisdom; they do not perceive an increase in feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness while practicing the perfection of wisdom. They do not perceive a decrease in form while practicing the perfection of wisdom; they do not perceive a decrease in feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness while practicing the perfection of wisdom. They do not perceive these as dharmas while practicing the perfection of wisdom, nor do they perceive them as non-dharmas while practicing the perfection of wisdom. Such a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing the perfection of wisdom, will swiftly attain its fulfillment."
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“That which the Tathāgata has spoken is inconceivable.
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"So it is! So it is! Because form is inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable; because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are inconceivable, that which is spoken by the Tathāgata is inconceivable."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, although they know form as it truly is to be inconceivable, they do not give rise to the notion of "inconceivability" as they practice the perfection of wisdom;

although they know feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as they truly are to be inconceivable, they do not give rise to the notion of "inconceivability" as they practice the perfection of wisdom. Such a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing the perfection of wisdom, will swiftly attain its full completion.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"The meaning and intent of this Prajñāpāramitā are so profoundly deep; who is able to believe and understand it?"
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śāriputra, saying:
“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva has long cultivated the great practice, they will be able to give rise to faith and understanding in this profound prajñāpāramitā.”
Then, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"To what extent should it be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva has long practiced the great path, such that he receives the designation 'one who has long practiced the great path'?"
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śāriputra, saying:

"When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they do not differentiate the ten powers of a Tathāgata; they do not differentiate the four fearlessnesses; they do not differentiate the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; they do not differentiate all-knowledge; and they do not differentiate the knowledge of all aspects."

Why is this? Because the Tathāgata’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all-knowledge, and the knowledge of all aspects are all inconceivable; likewise, all phenomena are also inconceivable.
Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices in this manner, they practice nowhere at all; this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), Śāriputra.

"In this regard, it should be known that these Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have long cultivated the Great Practice, and thus they have obtained the title 'those who have long cultivated the Great Practice.
The Venerable Subhūti then addressed the Buddha, saying:

"In this way, the Perfection of Wisdom is most profound; in this way, the Perfection of Wisdom is a great mass of jewels; in this way, the Perfection of Wisdom is a mass of purity, because it is as utterly pure as the great expanse of space."
The Buddha told Subhūti: "So it is! So it is!"
At that time, Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“It is marvelous,
World-Honored One!”
"In this way, although the Perfection of Wisdom is most profound and beset by many obstacles, now that it is being extensively taught, no obstacles shall arise.
The Buddha told Subhūti: "It is so! It is so!"
It is so! By the spiritual power of the Buddha, obstacles shall not arise.

Therefore, sons of good family who practice the Mahāyāna, if they wish to copy, receive and uphold, read and recite, cultivate, contemplate, or explain to others this profound Prajñāpāramitā, they should quickly copy it, and so forth, up to explaining it.
Why is this? Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* encounters many obstacles; do not allow it to fail in reaching its completion, whether in being written down or even in being expounded.

Subhūti, you should know that if such sons of good family of the Mahāyāna wish to write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, contemplate, and explain this profound *prajñāpāramitā* for one month or even up to one year and bring it to completion, they should apply themselves with diligent vigor, maintaining mindfulness as they write down and so forth until they explain it, so that they may reach its ultimate fulfillment over that period of time.
"Why is this? Because the great jewel of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* encounters many obstacles.
At that time, Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Rare indeed, World-Honored One!

This great jewel of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is beset by many obstacles. Yet, there are those who copy it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, practice and contemplate it, and explain it to others; against them, Māra the Evil One creates obstacles, preventing them from copying it, up to and including explaining it.”
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"Although Māra, the evil one, constantly seeks opportunities to create obstacles to this profound *prajñāpāramitā*—desiring to prevent its transcription up to its exposition—he lacks the power to create such obstacles so as to cause the bodhisattva’s undertaking to fail."
Then, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“By whose spiritual power is it that those evil Māras are unable to obstruct these bodhisattvas in their activities such as copying [the sūtras]?”
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śāriputra, saying:
“It is through the supernatural power of the Buddha that those evil Māras are unable to obstruct or hinder those bodhisattvas in their activities such as transcribing [the sūtras].”
Furthermore, Śāriputra!

It is also through the spiritual power of all Buddhas in the worlds of the ten directions that those evil Māras are unable to obstruct or hinder those bodhisattvas in their activities such as transcribing [the scriptures].
Furthermore, Śāriputra!
Because all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas collectively protect and keep in mind those bodhisattvas who practice the profound Prajñāpāramitā, Māra the Evil One is unable to obstruct them.
Why is this? Śāriputra, all the Buddhas,

the World-Honored Ones, together protect and keep in mind the wholesome deeds performed by those bodhisattvas who practice the profound perfection of wisdom, so that those evil Māras cannot obstruct them.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!

If bodhisattvas write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, contemplate, and expound this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, it is the natural law that they shall be protected and remembered by all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently teaching the Dharma throughout the worlds of the ten directions. If they are protected and remembered by those Buddhas, it is the natural law that the māras and their followers will be unable to obstruct them.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!
If there are sons of good family with pure faith who write down, receive and uphold, read, recite, practice, contemplate, and expound this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they should form this thought:

"That I am now writing down, and so forth, up to expounding this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, is entirely due to the protective mindfulness and spiritual power of all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, throughout the worlds of the ten directions."
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:

“If sons of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle write down, receive, uphold, recite, practice, contemplate, and expound this profound perfection of wisdom, all of this is due to the spiritual power, compassion, and protective mindfulness of the Buddhas of the ten directions, which causes their sublime and virtuous deeds to be unable to be obstructed by the followers of Māra.”
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śāriputra, saying: “So it is! So it is!”
"It is as you have said.
Then, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:

"If sons of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, contemplate, and expound this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in the worlds of the ten directions will collectively recognize them, rejoice in them, and protect them with mindfulness."

The Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, of the worlds in the ten directions constantly behold them all together with their Buddha-eyes, compassionately protecting and mindful of them, so that whatever they practice shall be accomplished without exception.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śāriputra, saying: "So it is! So it is!"
It is as you have said.

If sons of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle write down, receive, uphold, read, recite, cultivate, contemplate, and explain this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they will at all times be seen, known, and protected by the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, with their Buddha-eyes throughout all worlds in the ten directions. Consequently, no evil Māras shall be able to disturb or afflict them, and all the wholesome deeds they perform shall be swiftly accomplished.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!

If sons of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle can write down, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, contemplate, and expound this profound Prajñāpāramitā, you should know that they have already drawn near to unsurpassed bodhi, and that no evil Māras or adversaries can obstruct them.
Furthermore, Śāriputra,

if sons of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle can write down this profound Prajñāpāramitā, adorn it in various ways, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, and offer it worship and respect, they will always be seen, known, and protected by the Tathāgata’s Buddha-eye.

By virtue of these causes and conditions, one will certainly obtain great wealth, great benefit, great fruits, and great retribution; furthermore, one shall attain the stage of non-retrogression, never be separated from the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, constantly hear the True Dharma, avoid falling into the evil realms, and experience various sublime joys among devas and humans.
Why is this? Śāriputra,

it is because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* enables all sentient beings to realize the ultimate meaning (*paramārtha*) of all phenomena as they truly are, thereby bringing about various kinds of benefit and happiness in both the present and the future.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

After my parinirvāṇa, these sūtras associated with the profound *prajñāpāramitā* shall gradually flourish in the southeast. In that region, there will be many sons of good family who abide in the bodhisattva vehicle and who, with deep faith and joy, are able to write down, receive and uphold, read, recite, practice, contemplate, and explain such sūtras associated with the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, and who shall offer them worship, reverence, respect, and praise."
After my parinirvāṇa, this sūtra will spread from the southeast to the south and gradually flourish there.

In that region, there will be many sons of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle and who, with deep resolve, will have faith in and delight in such profound sūtras associated with the Prajñāpāramitā; they will write them down, receive and uphold them, read and recite them, practice and contemplate them, explain them, and offer them worship, respect, honor, and praise.

After my parinirvāṇa, these sūtras will further flourish, spreading gradually from the south to the southwest. In that region, there will be many sons of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle and who, with deep resolve and joyful faith, will write down, uphold, read, recite, practice, contemplate, and explain such profound sūtras associated with the Prajñāpāramitā; they will also make offerings to them, honoring, respecting, revering, and praising them.

After my parinirvāṇa, such sūtras as these shall gradually flourish from the southwest to the northwest. In that region, there will be many sons of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle and who, with deep resolve, will have faith in and delight in sūtras corresponding to this profound Prajñāpāramitā; they will copy, receive and uphold, read and recite, cultivate, contemplate, and expound them, and they will make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise them.

After my parinirvāṇa, this sūtra will gradually flourish as it moves from the northwest to the north. In that region, there will be many sons of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle and who, with deep resolve, will have faith and joy in such profound sūtras associated with the Prajñāpāramitā; they will copy, uphold, read, recite, practice, contemplate, and explain them, and will offer them worship, honor, respect, and praise.

After my parinirvāṇa, this sūtra will further flourish, spreading gradually from the north to the northeast. In that region, there will be many sons of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle and who, with deep faith and joy, will write down, receive, uphold, read, recite, practice, contemplate, and explain such profound sūtras associated with the Prajñāpāramitā; they will also make offerings to them, honoring, respecting, revering, and praising them.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

After my parinirvāṇa, in a later time, a later period, during the final five hundred years, sūtras associated with the profound Prajñāpāramitā will perform great Buddha-work in the northeastern region."
Why is this? Śāriputra,

the sūtras associated with the profound Prajñāpāramitā are collectively revered by all Tathāgatas and collectively protected and sustained by all Tathāgatas, so that they shall not perish for a long time in those regions.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, the unsurpassed true Dharma of the Vinaya attained by the Buddhas does not possess the characteristic of extinction or disappearance; that unsurpassed true Dharma of the Vinaya attained by the Buddhas is precisely the sūtras associated with the Prajñāpāramitā.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!

Those sons of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who dwell in the northeast, who are able to have deep faith and joy in this profound sūtra associated with the perfection of wisdom, and who copy it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, practice it, contemplate it, explain it, and honor, revere, respect, and praise it—[they shall attain great merit].

"We, the Buddhas, shall constantly behold and protect you with our Buddha-eyes, ensuring that you suffer no harm or affliction, so that your body and mind may remain peaceful and happy in the present and the future.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:

"After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, during the later period, the subsequent age, and the final five hundred years, will this sūtra associated with the profound Prajñāpāramitā be widely disseminated in the northeast?"
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śāriputra, saying: “So it is! So it is!”

Śāriputra! After my parinirvāṇa, in a later time, a later period, during the final five hundred years, those sons of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle in the northeastern quarter, if they hear this profound sūtra associated with the perfection of wisdom and, with deep resolve, believe in and delight in it—copying it, receiving and upholding it, reading and reciting it, practicing it, contemplating it, and explaining it—and if they honor, revere, respect, and praise it; [they shall attain great merit].

It should be known that such a person has long since resolved upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment; has long cultivated the practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva; has made offerings to many Buddhas and served many virtuous friends; and has long practiced the discipline of body, speech, and mind, as well as wisdom. All the roots of virtue they have planted have already reached maturity. By the power of this merit, they are able to hear this profound sūtra associated with the *prajñāpāramitā* and, with deep resolve, believe in and delight in it; furthermore, they are able to write it down, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it, contemplate it according to the principle, and extensively explain and analyze it for the sake of sentient beings.
At that time, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:

“After the Buddha has entered parinirvāṇa, in a later time, a later period, during the final five hundred years when the Dharma is about to perish, how many sons of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle will there be in the northeast who, upon hearing such profound sūtras associated with the Prajñāpāramitā, will with deep resolve believe and rejoice in them, and furthermore be able to write them down, receive and uphold them, read and recite them, practice and cultivate them, contemplate them, and explain them to others, while making offerings to, honoring, respecting, and praising them?”
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śāriputra, saying:

“After my parinirvāṇa, in a later time, a later period, during the final five hundred years when the Dharma is about to perish, although there may be immeasurable sons of good family dwelling in the Bodhisattva vehicle in the northeastern region, few will hear the sūtras associated with the profound *prajñāpāramitā* and, with deep hearts, believe in and delight in them; furthermore, they will be able to write them down, receive and uphold them, read and recite them, practice and cultivate them, contemplate them, and explain them to others, as well as making offerings to, honoring, respecting, and praising them.”

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when sons of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle hear such profound sūtras associated with the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), their minds do not sink; they are not startled, not terrified, and they give rise to deep faith and delight. They copy, receive and uphold, read and recite, practice, contemplate, and explain them; and they make offerings to, revere, respect, and praise them."

It should be known that this person has already personally approached, made offerings to, honored, revered, and praised immeasurable Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and Bodhisattvas, and has inquired about the profound meaning and intent of the Prajñāpāramitā.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

These sons of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle will, before long, certainly fulfill the path of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. Because they are protected and remembered by all Tathāgatas, because they are sustained by immeasurable spiritual friends, and because they are upheld by superior roots of goodness, they shall swiftly realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment for the sake of benefiting many sentient beings."

Why is this? Śāriputra, I constantly teach the Dharma associated with omniscience to those sons of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle; likewise, the Tathāgatas of the past also constantly taught them the Dharma associated with omniscience.

By virtue of these causes and conditions, in future lives they will be able to constantly cultivate and accumulate the correct practice associated with the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), swiftly proceeding toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*). They will also be able to preach the Dharma to others as appropriate, leading them toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. At all times, their body and mind will remain stable; even the Evil Māra and his retinue will be unable to destroy their resolve to seek unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, let alone other evildoers who delight in malice and disparage the *prajñāpāramitā* and attempt to obstruct their minds, preventing them from striving diligently for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment!
Why is this? Because their courageous and correct diligence toward unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment is extremely firm.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!

Sons of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle, upon hearing this profound *prajñāpāramitā* being taught, attain a vast and pure joy in their hearts; they are also able to establish immeasurable sentient beings in sublime wholesome dharmas, leading them toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Why is this? Śāriputra!
These sons of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle have now, in my presence, made great vows of aspiration:

"I shall establish immeasurable hundreds of thousands of sentient beings, causing them to resolve upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, to practice the various deeds of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and by demonstrating, exhorting, encouraging, and inspiring them, lead them to unexcelled, perfect, and complete bodhi, even unto receiving the prediction of non-retrogression."
I felt profound sympathetic joy toward that aspiration.
Why is this? Śāriputra!

I observe that the person’s aspiration is such that their mind and speech are in accord; in the future, they will certainly be able to establish immeasurable hundreds of thousands of sentient beings, causing them to resolve upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, to cultivate the practices of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas, and to be shown, exhorted, encouraged, and gladdened, until they receive the prediction of non-retrogression regarding unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"These sons of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva Vehicle also, in the presence of immeasurable Buddhas of the past, made this great vow:
'I shall establish immeasurable hundreds of thousands of sentient beings, causing them to resolve upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment;

I shall cause them to cultivate the practices of the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, and by manifesting, exhorting, encouraging, and gladdening them, I shall lead them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment until they receive the prediction of non-retrogression.'"
The Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past also deeply rejoiced in that aspiration.
Why is this? Śāriputra!

The Buddhas of the past likewise observed that the noble vows and the words of those sons of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle are in accord with their resolve; they will certainly, in the future, establish immeasurable hundreds of thousands of sentient beings, causing them to generate the mind set on unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, to cultivate the practices of the bodhisattvas mahāsattvas, and by demonstrating, exhorting, inspiring, and gladdening them, lead them to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, even unto receiving the prediction of non-retrogression.

"These sons of noble family belonging to the Bodhisattva Vehicle have faith and understanding in the vast, and they practice the vast path; they aspire to be born in the Buddha-fields of other directions where Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently reside and proclaim such a supreme Dharma as this profound Prajñāpāramitā."

Having heard this unsurpassed Dharma of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, he is further able to establish countless hundreds of thousands of sentient beings within that buddha-field, causing them to resolve upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*), to cultivate the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and—by means of demonstration, exhortation, encouragement, and inspiration—to cause them to attain non-retrogression from unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“How extraordinary,
World-Honored One!”

The Buddha has fully realized and awakened to all phenomena of the past, future, and present, such that there is nothing he does not know and nothing he does not perceive. He has fully realized and awakened to the diverse mental activities of all sentient beings, such that there is nothing he does not know and nothing he does not perceive. He has fully realized and awakened to the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, and Buddha-fields of the three periods of time, such that there is nothing he does not know and nothing he does not perceive.
"Bhagavān!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to listen with a sincere heart to this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it, reflect upon it according to the principle, transcribe it, explain it, and cause it to spread widely, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva, in future lives, will always seek out the sūtras associated with the *prajñāpāramitā* with courageous diligence, never ceasing."
"In those sūtras associated with the Prajñāpāramitā, is there a time when one attains [realization] and a time when one does not?
At that time, the Buddha said to Śāriputra: "It is so!"
It is so! There is nothing that the Buddha does not realize or know, and nothing he does not fully awaken to.

This bodhisattva mahāsattva constantly seeks with courageous diligence and tireless joy the sūtras associated with the *prajñāpāramitā*; at all times they are obtained, and there is no time when they are not obtained.
Why is this? Śāriputra,

it is because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas constantly and tirelessly seek out the sūtras associated with the *prajñāpāramitā*, for they are always protected and remembered by all buddhas and bodhisattvas.
Then, Śāriputra again addressed the Buddha, saying:

"Does this bodhisattva mahāsattva only obtain these sūtras associated with the profound perfection of wisdom through persistent and heroic diligence, seeking them without ceasing so that they are obtained at all times and there is never a time when they are not obtained, or can he also constantly obtain other sūtras?"
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śāriputra, saying:

“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva always seeks the sūtras associated with the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) with courageous faith, disregarding even their own body and life, it is impossible that they should at times fail to obtain other sūtras.”
Why is this? Śāriputra, it is because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,

seeking unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, manifest themselves to, exhort, encourage, and gladden all sentient beings, causing them to receive, uphold, read, recite, contemplate, and practice the sūtras associated with the perfection of wisdom as well as other sūtras.

By virtue of these roots of goodness, wherever they are born, it is the natural law that they shall always receive, uphold, read, and recite the profound *Prajñāpāramitā* sūtras corresponding to emptiness, as well as other scriptures.
Chapter Eleven: On the Works of Māra, Part One. At that time, Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”

It has already been stated that when sons of good family and others who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle cultivate meritorious qualities, there are many obstacles. What are these things called "obstacles"?
The Buddha told Subhūti:
"Obstacles refer to the deeds of Māra."
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha,
saying, "What is called the work of Māra for a bodhisattva?
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva, when wishing to proclaim the *prajñāpāramitā*, finds that eloquence regarding the essential teachings of the Dharma arises only after a long time, or if eloquence regarding the essential teachings of the Dharma suddenly arises at the very end, or if eloquence regarding the essential teachings of the Dharma arises in excessive measure, or if he stops before what he wishes to say is exhausted, or if his speech regarding the essential teachings of the Dharma is confused and jumbled, or if his speech regarding the essential teachings of the Dharma is interrupted, or if various adverse events arise while he is teaching, causing him not to fulfill his original intention in what he wishes to say—one should know these to be the deeds of Māra for a bodhisattva."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva is copying the profound sūtra of the *prajñāpāramitā*, if they yawn repeatedly, or laugh at one another, or treat each other with contempt, or their body and mind are restless and agitated, or they lose mindfulness and become distracted, or the text and phrases are inverted, or they are confused about the meaning and principles, or they fail to find its flavor and give rise to weariness and abandonment, or if sudden calamities arise, or they quarrel and dispute with one another—due to such matters, if the copying is not brought to completion, you should know that these are the deeds of Māra for a bodhisattva."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva receives, upholds, recites, contemplates, practices, explains, or listens to this profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra, if they yawn frequently, or mock one another, or treat each other with contempt, or their body and mind become restless and agitated, or they lose mindfulness and become distracted, or the words and phrases are inverted, or they are confused regarding the principles, or they fail to find its flavor and their minds give rise to weariness and abandonment, or sudden calamities arise, or they engage in mutual strife—know that because of such matters, what they undertake will not be accomplished; these should be understood as the deeds of Māra for a bodhisattva."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
If, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva hears the profound sūtras of the Prajñāpāramitā being preached, they should think:
'I have not received a prediction regarding this; what is the use of listening? "
Or they may think:
"My name is not mentioned here; what is the use of listening?
Or they may think:
"In this [teaching], my place of birth—whether city or village—is not mentioned; what use is there in listening to it?

Due to such causes and conditions, their minds become unpurified; they rise from their seats and depart with aversion and renunciation, lacking any sense of attachment or longing. One should know that this constitutes a demonic obstacle for a bodhisattva.
Subhūti, you should know this:

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing the profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtra being expounded, has a mind that is not pure and abandons it with aversion, then according to the number of steps taken while harboring such an impure and averse mind toward this sūtra, he shall lose that many eons of merit and incur the transgression of obstructing enlightenment for that many eons.

Having experienced those karmic retributions, one must again exert diligent effort for that same duration to practice the various difficult and painful austerities of a bodhisattva before being able to restore one's original state; therefore, this is called a demonic activity of a bodhisattva.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva abandons the sūtras associated with the profound *prajñāpāramitā* that lead to the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*), and instead studies other sūtras that do not lead to the knowledge of all modes but conform to the two vehicles, abandoning the root to grasp at branches and leaves—this should be known as a deed of Māra for a bodhisattva."

Why is this? Because the sūtras associated with the profound *prajñāpāramitā* can generate the mundane and supramundane, preeminent merits of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; by means of these, they can induce the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*) and possess great power and function, just like the roots of a tree.
No other sūtras possess such efficacy; they are like branches and leaves that lack superior power.

If sons of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle study such profound sūtras associated with the *prajñāpāramitā*, they are thereby studying all the mundane and supramundane sublime qualities of the assembly of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and will swiftly be able to bring forth the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*).

If sons of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle should abandon such sūtras associated with the profound perfection of wisdom and instead seek to study sūtras associated with the two vehicles, they are thereby abandoning all the mundane and supramundane sublime merits of the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and will ultimately be unable to attain the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

These sons of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva Vehicle have meager merit and wisdom; they abandon the root and seek the branches. For this reason, it is called a demonic deed of a bodhisattva.
"Subhūti, you should know this!"

Just as a foolish, starving dog abandons its own staple food to instead beg for scraps from a servant, so too will there be sons of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle in future ages who abandon the profound sūtras associated with the perfection of wisdom—the very root of the knowledge of all modes—and instead seek to study sūtras associated with the two vehicles; it is exactly like this.

Why is this? Because these sons of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle possess dull and obtuse wisdom; having abandoned the profound *prajñāpāramitā* sūtras associated with the attainment of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), they seek to study the sūtras that lead to the qualities of Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, and thus they will certainly not attain the knowledge of all modes.

Why is this so? The sūtras associated with the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas are intended solely for the sake of one's own self-discipline and tranquility, for emerging from the suffering of saṃsāra and attaining the bliss of nirvāṇa. By diligently studying such sūtras, the roots of virtue they induce ultimately result only in abiding on the levels of the two vehicles, wherein the fulfillment of one's own benefit is attained.

The sutras associated with the profound *prajñāpāramitā* universally rescue all sentient beings from the suffering of birth and death so that they may attain the bliss of *nirvāṇa*. By diligently practicing and studying these sutras, the roots of goodness they induce will ultimately enable one to attain the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñājñāna*), thereby benefiting and bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

It is as if there were a person who, wishing to observe the size of a fragrant elephant's body and the excellence or inferiority of its physical characteristics, having obtained [the elephant] itself, does not observe it but instead seeks out its tracks."
"What do you think?
Is that person wise?
Subhūti replied:
"No, World-Honored One!
The Buddha said to Subhūti:

"In a future age, there will be sons of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle who abandon the profound sūtras associated with the perfection of wisdom—the very root of omniscient wisdom—and instead seek to study sūtras associated with the two vehicles, hoping therein to attain omniscient wisdom; they shall be just like this."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

It is as if there were a person who, for the sake of precious jewels, set out for the great ocean; yet having reached the shore, instead of entering the great ocean, he looked back at a cow’s footprint and thought to himself:
'How could the measure of the water in the great ocean, so deep and vast, possibly compare to this?'"
"There should also be various precious jewels within this.
What do you think?
Is that person wise?"
Subhūti replied,
“No, World-Honored One!”
The Buddha told Subhūti:

“In a future age, there will be sons of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who abandon the sūtras associated with the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, the root of all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), and instead seek to study sūtras associated with the two vehicles, hoping therein to attain all-knowledge; it shall be just like this.”

Why is this? Because even if one diligently studies and practices the sūtras of the two vehicles, at best one can only attain the fruit of stream-entry, and by successive stages reach up to the enlightenment of a pratyekabuddha; one will certainly be unable to attain the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).

Therefore, sons of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle who wish to swiftly realize the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) should study the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), and should not seek to study the scriptures of the two vehicles.
Why is this? Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is definitively the root of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), whereas the sūtras of the two vehicles are like branches and leaves.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

It is as if there were a master carpenter or his disciple who, wishing to construct a great palace equal in scale to the magnificent palace of Śakra, Lord of the Devas, were to see that palace and instead take the palaces of the sun and moon as their model."
"What do you think?
Could such a craftsman or his apprentice build a great hall equal in measure to the sublime palace of Śakra?
Subhūti replied:
"No, World-Honored One!
The Buddha said to Subhūti:
"Is that person wise?
Subhūti replied,
"That person is not wise."
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"In a future age, there will be sons of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who, having obtained this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, abandon it to seek and study the scriptures of the two vehicles, desiring to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to sentient beings. They, too, are just like this; you should know that they belong to the class of the deluded."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

It is as if someone who wishes to see a wheel-turning monarch (cakravartin), having seen him but failing to recognize him, leaves him and goes elsewhere; there he sees a minor king and, observing his physical appearance, thinks to himself:
'How could the physical appearance and majestic power of a wheel-turning monarch possibly surpass this?'"
"What do you think?
Is that person wise?
Subhūti replied:
"No, World-Honored One!
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"In future ages, there will be sons of noble family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who, desiring to proceed toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and to turn the sublime wheel of Dharma to deliver the multitudes of sentient beings, will abandon the profound *prajñāpāramitā* and seek to study sūtras associated with the two vehicles, saying:
