Is it possible to practice emptiness by means of attaining some dharma apart from emptiness? “It is not so!”
“Excellent, Subhūti!
‘World-Honored One,
is it precisely the perfection of wisdom that is able to practice emptiness?’”
"No, World-Honored One!
Subhūti, it is not so.
"World-Honored One! [Subhūti replied.]
“Is there any dharma to be obtained apart from the perfection of wisdom that can practice emptiness?
“Not so, Subhūti!”
“World-Honored One!
Is it form itself that can practice the perfection of wisdom? “No, it is not.”
"Subhūti!
"World-Honored One!
Is there any dharma apart from form that can be apprehended which is able to practice the perfection of wisdom?"
"No, World-Honored One!
Subhūti, it is not so.
"World-Honored One! [Subhūti replied.]
"Is it that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness themselves can practice the perfection of wisdom?
"No, Subhūti!"
“World-Honored One!
Is there any dharma apart from feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness that can practice the perfection of wisdom? “It is not so.”
"Subhūti!
"World-Honored One!
Is it that form itself is emptiness which is able to practice the perfection of wisdom?"
"No, World-Honored One!
Subhūti, it is not so.
"World-Honored One! [Subhūti replied.]
“Can one who perceives a dharma as existing apart from form and emptiness practice the perfection of wisdom?
“No, Subhūti!”
“World-Honored One!
Is it by means of the emptiness of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness that one is able to practice the perfection of wisdom? “It is not so.”
“Subhūti!
‘World-Honored One!
Is there any dharma to be found that is separate from the emptiness of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, which is able to practice the perfection of wisdom?’”
"No, World-Honored One!
Subhūti, it is not so.
"World-Honored One! [Subhūti replied.]
“Can one who is identical with form practice emptiness?
“Not so, Subhūti!”
“World-Honored One!
Is there any dharma apart from form that can be apprehended which is able to practice emptiness? “It is not so.”
“Subhūti!
‘World-Honored One!
Is it that feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness themselves can practice emptiness?’”
“No, World-Honored One!
Subhūti, it is not so.
“World-Honored One! [Subhūti replied.]
"Can one who is free from the apprehension of dharmas apart from feeling, perception, mental formations,
and consciousness practice emptiness?
"No, Subhūti!"
“World-Honored One!
Is it that form itself is emptiness, and can one practice emptiness? “It is not so.”
"Subhūti!
"World-Honored One!
Is there any dharma to be found apart from the emptiness of form that can practice emptiness?"
"No, World-Honored One!
Subhūti, it is not so.
"World-Honored One! [Subhūti replied.]
"Is it that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are themselves empty,
and thus able to practice emptiness?
"No, Subhūti!"
“World-Honored One!
Is there any dharma to be obtained that is separate from the emptiness of feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, which can practice emptiness? “It is not so!”
“Subhūti!
“World-Honored One!
Is it that all dharmas themselves are able to practice the perfection of wisdom?”
"No, World-Honored One!
Subhūti, [it is not so].
"World-Honored One!"
“Can one practice the perfection of wisdom by way of abandoning the apprehension of any dharma as a real entity?
“No, Subhūti.”
“World-Honored One!
Is it that the emptiness of all phenomena itself can practice the perfection of wisdom? “It is not so.”
"Subhūti!
"World-Honored One!
Is there any dharma that can be apprehended apart from the emptiness of all dharmas, such that one could practice the perfection of wisdom?"
"No, World-Honored One!
Subhūti, it is not so.
"World-Honored One! [Subhūti replied.]
"Is it that all phenomena themselves are able to practice emptiness?
"No, Subhūti!"
“World-Honored One!
Is it by being detached from all dharmas that one can practice emptiness while having something obtainable? “It is not so!”
"Subhūti!
"World-Honored One!
Is it that very emptiness of all phenomena that is able to practice emptiness?"
"No, World-Honored One!
Subhūti, [it is not so].
"World-Honored One! [Subhūti replied.]
"In order to be free from the notion that there is a dharma to be apprehived within the emptiness of all dharmas,
can one practice emptiness?
"No, Subhūti!"
At that time, Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"If that is so, by what dharmas do bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom and practice emptiness?"
The Buddha said to Subhūti:
"What do you think?
Do you perceive any dharma that can practice the perfection of wisdom or that can practice emptiness?"
Subhūti replied,
“No, World-Honored One!”
The Buddha said to Subhūti:
"What do you think?
Do you perceive a prajñāpāramitā, or do you perceive an emptiness that constitutes the sphere of activity for a bodhisattva mahāsattva?"
Subhūti replied,
“No, World-Honored One!”
The Buddha said to Subhūti:
"What do you think?
Is that dharma which you do not perceive obtainable as a dharma?"
Subhūti replied,
“No, World-Honored One!”
The Buddha said to Subhūti:
"What do you think?
Do dharmas that cannot be apprehended have arising and ceasing?"
Subhūti replied,
"No, World-Honored One!"
The Buddha told Subhūti:
"That true mark of all dharmas which you do not see and do not apprehend is precisely the bodhisattva’s patience regarding the non-arising of dharmas."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes such non-arising dharma-patience (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti), they are then capable of receiving the prediction (vyākaraṇa) regarding unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
Subhūti, you should know this!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva, regarding the Buddha’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, four unhindered understandings, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, and the eighteen unique qualities of a buddha—these immeasurable and boundless, supreme merits—is called one who is able to practice with diligence according to reality.

If one can practice with such diligence, it is impossible that they should not attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening wisdom, the wisdom of all aspects, great wisdom, sublime wisdom, the wisdom of all-knowledge, and the wisdom of the great caravan leader.
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Do all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas receive the prediction of their attainment of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment by virtue of the non-arising nature of all phenomena?"
"No, World-Honored One!
Subhūti, it is not so.
"World-Honored One! [Subhūti replied.]

"Do all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas receive the prediction of their attainment of the Buddha's unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment by virtue of the fact that all phenomena possess the nature of arising? "No, they do not."
“Subhūti!
‘World-Honored One!

Do all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas receive the prediction of their attainment of the Buddha’s unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment by means of the dharma-nature of all phenomena, whether they have arisen or have not arisen?’”
"No, World-Honored One!
Subhūti, it is not so.
"World-Honored One! [Subhūti replied.]

Do the bodhisattva mahāsattvas receive the prediction of their attainment of the Buddha’s unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment by virtue of the fact that all phenomena have neither the nature of arising nor the nature of non-arising?
"No, Subhūti! At that time, Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“If that is so, how is it that bodhisattva mahāsattvas are capable of receiving the prediction regarding the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of a Buddha?
The Buddha said to Subhūti:
“What do you think?”
"Do you see any dharma that receives the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect,
and complete enlightenment from the Buddha? Subhūti replied, "No!"
"Bhagavān!

I do not perceive any dharma that is capable of receiving the prediction for the Buddha’s unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; nor do I perceive any dharma that is able to realize the Buddha’s unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Furthermore, I do not perceive the time of realization, the place of realization, or the dharma realized by means of which it is realized."
Why is this? Because all phenomena are unattainable;

within the unattainability of all phenomena, the one who realizes, that which is realized, the time of realization, the place of realization, and the means by which it is realized are all unattainable.
The Buddha told Subhūti: "So it is! So it is!"
"It is as you have said.
Subhūti, you should know that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not apprehend any phenomenon, they do not form such a thought:"

"I shall be able to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; by means of this dharma, at such a time, and in such a place, I shall realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
23. Chapter on the Lord of Devas, Part Four, Chapter Twenty-three. At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
"In this way, the perfection of wisdom is most profound, difficult to see, and difficult to realize.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of Devas, saying:
"It is so! It is so!"
"So it is! It is just as you have said, Kauśika!"
In this way, the perfection of wisdom is most profound; in this way, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to see and difficult to realize, Kausika!
Because space is profoundly deep, this Prajñāpāramitā is most profound; because space is difficult to see and difficult to realize, this Prajñāpāramitā is difficult to see and difficult to realize.
Why is this? Kauśika!
Because the intrinsic nature of this prajñāpāramitā is utterly remote and non-existent, being like empty space.
Then, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, again addressed the Buddha, saying:

“Sentient beings who possess no small amount of roots of virtue are able to listen with a sincere heart to this profound Prajñāpāramitā—which is difficult to see and difficult to realize—receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently study and practice it, contemplate it according to the principle, and extensively analyze and explain it for the sake of sentient beings.”
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of Devas, saying: “So it is! So it is!”
"It is as you have said, Kauśika!

It is not possible for sentient beings who possess only a small amount of roots of virtue to wholeheartedly hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to the principle, and extensively analyze and explain to others this profound Prajñāpāramitā—which is so difficult to see and difficult to realize—or to be able to transcribe it and cause it to circulate widely. The merit of these sentient beings is immeasurable."
“Kauśika! Suppose that every single sentient being within this Jambudvīpa were to fully accomplish the ten paths of wholesome action.
What do you think?”
"Are the merits of these sentient beings great?
Śakra, Lord of Devas, replied:
"They are very great!"
“World-Honored One!
It is very much so! Sugata!”

The Buddha said, "Kauśika! If there are sons of good family or daughters of good family who, regarding this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, listen with a sincere heart, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, diligently practice and study it, contemplate it according to the principle, and extensively explain it for the sake of sentient beings— or if they are able to transcribe it and cause it to circulate widely— the mass of merit obtained by these sons and daughters of good family surpasses the aforementioned merit a hundredfold, a thousandfold, and even up to an *upaniṣad*-fold."
At that time, a bhikṣu in the assembly said to Śakra, the Lord of Devas: “Kauśika!

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family should, with a sincere heart, hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to the principle, and extensively explain and analyze for the sake of sentient beings this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā—or even write it down and cause it to be widely circulated—the mass of merit obtained by such sons and daughters of good family would surpass yours.”
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, said:

"These sons and daughters of good family surpass even me at the very first moment they resolve their minds toward enlightenment; how much more so when they wholeheartedly hear, receive, uphold, read, recite, diligently practice, reflect upon according to the principle, and extensively analyze and explain for the sake of sentient beings this profound sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā, or even transcribe it and cause it to circulate widely!"
“Bhikṣus, you should know that the mass of merit obtained by this bodhisattva mahāsattva also surpasses all the qualities possessed by the gods, humans, and asuras of the entire world.”
“Bhikṣus, you should know!

The mass of merit obtained by this bodhisattva mahāsattva not only surpasses all the merits of the world’s devas, humans, and asuras, but it also surpasses all the merits of stream-enterers, once-returners, non-returners, arhats, and pratyekabuddhas.”
“Bhikṣus, you should know!

The mass of merit acquired by this bodhisattva mahāsattva not only surpasses all the virtues of stream-enterers, once-returners, non-returners, arhats, and pratyekabuddhas, but also surpasses all bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, being devoid of the skillful means of the perfection of wisdom, practice generosity as great donors.”
“Bhikṣus, you should know!

The mass of merit acquired by this bodhisattva mahāsattva also surpasses that of all other bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, being devoid of the skillful means of the perfection of wisdom, constantly cultivate and train in pure ethical discipline—ethical discipline that is unimpaired, unblemished, unmixed, untainted, and the complete aggregate of morality.”
“Bhikṣus, you should know!

The mass of merit obtained by this bodhisattva mahāsattva also surpasses that of all other bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, though devoid of the skillful means of the perfection of wisdom, have constantly practiced and mastered perfect patience, perfect tranquility, freedom from malice and resentment, and even ultimate patience such that they harbor no thought of harm toward even a piece of scorched wood.
“Bhikṣus, you should know!

The mass of merit obtained by this bodhisattva mahāsattva surpasses that of all other bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, though devoid of the skillful means of the perfection of wisdom, constantly practice with courageous diligence, do not abandon the yoke of virtue, are neither indolent nor discouraged, and possess the perfect diligence of body, speech, and mind.”
“Bhikṣus, you should know!

The mass of merit obtained by this bodhisattva mahāsattva also surpasses that of all other bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, being devoid of the skillful means of the perfection of wisdom, constantly practice and study the meditative concentrations that are desirable, delightful, heroic, stable, sovereign, and perfect.”
“Bhikṣus, you should know!

The mass of merit acquired by this bodhisattva mahāsattva also surpasses all other roots of goodness constantly cultivated and studied by bodhisattva mahāsattvas who are devoid of the skillful means of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).”

“Bhikṣus, you should know that because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom as it has been taught and possesses skillful means, they surpass all those in the world— gods, humans, and asuras— and they also surpass all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, as well as all bodhisattvas who are devoid of the perfection of wisdom and skillful means.”
Why is this? Because this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound *prajñāpāramitā* as it has been taught, and follows along with the profound *prajñāpāramitā* to its ultimate conclusion.

This bodhisattva-mahāsattva is able to perpetuate the lineage of the knowledge of all-knowledge so that it remains uninterrupted, and is never separated from the Buddhas, bodhisattvas, and true, pure, virtuous friends.
This bodhisattva mahāsattva thus practices such sublime and pure conduct, never departing from the wondrous seat of enlightenment, subduing all māras and restraining all heterodox teachers.
When these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas train in this way, they possess skillful means and are constantly able to rescue and deliver all sentient beings who are mired in the mud of afflictions.

When these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas train in this way, they possess skillful means and constantly study the dharmas that the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should study, rather than studying the dharmas that those of the Śrāvaka and Pratyekabuddha vehicles should study.
“Bhikṣus, you should know!

When these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas train in this way in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, the hosts of devas all rejoice greatly. The Four Great Kings who protect the world, each leading their own celestial hosts, come to where they are, making offerings, paying homage, honoring, and praising them, all saying:
‘Excellent!’”
"O Mahāsattva!

You should diligently apply yourself with vigor to study the dharmas that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas ought to study; do not study the dharmas that those of the śrāvaka and pratyekabuddha vehicles ought to study. If you study in this manner, you shall swiftly and securely sit upon the sublime seat of awakening and quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
Just as the previous Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas accepted the four bowls offered by the Four Heavenly Kings, you too should accept them;
and just as in the past the Four Great World-Protecting Kings presented four bowls, I too shall present them.

“Bhikṣus, you should know that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, even we, the Lord of Devas, lead the host of devas to his presence to make offerings, pay homage, show respect, and offer praise; how much more so would other celestial deities not go to his presence!”

“Bhikṣus, you should know that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, as well as the assembly of bodhisattva mahāsattvas, together with the devas, nāgas, asuras, and others, will constantly follow, protect, and keep them in mind.”

By virtue of these causes and conditions, this bodhisattva-mahāsattva cannot be harmed by any of the perils, calamities, or physical and mental sufferings of the world; all manner of diseases arising from the disharmony of the four great elements that exist in the world shall never exist within his body, except for those heavy karmic deeds which are transformed and manifested as light retributions.
“Bhikṣus, you should know!

This bodhisattva mahāsattva, through practicing the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) with skillful means (upāyakauśalya) as taught, attains such immeasurable and boundless merits in both the present life and future lives.”
At that time, Ānanda had this thought to himself:

"Is it by his own eloquence that Śakra, Lord of the Devas, praises and speaks thus of the profound perfection of wisdom and the merits and benefits of the bodhisattvas, or is it through the majestic spiritual power of the Tathāgata?"
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, receiving the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power and knowing the thoughts in Ānanda’s mind, addressed him, saying:
"Virtuous One!
That which I have praised and described—the profound *prajñāpāramitā* and the merits and benefits of all bodhisattvas—are entirely due to the majestic spiritual power of the Tathāgata."
At that time, the Buddha said to Ānanda: "So it is! So it is!"

When Śakra, Lord of the Devas, thus praises and speaks of the merits and benefits of this profound perfection of wisdom and of all bodhisattvas, you should know that these are entirely through the supernatural power of the Tathāgata, and not through his own eloquence.

Why is this? Because the merit and supreme excellence of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* and the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are certainly beyond the capacity of all those in the world—gods, humans, asuras, and others—to praise or describe.
Chapter 24: On Being Unmixed and Undifferentiated, Part Four, Section 24: On Being Unmixed and Undifferentiated. At that time, the Buddha addressed Ānanda, saying:
"When a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates the *prajñāpāramitā*, studies the *prajñāpāramitā*, and practices the *prajñāpāramitā*..."
At that time, all the evil Māras in the trichiliocosm were filled with doubt and all thought to themselves:
"Will this bodhisattva mahāsattva realize the limit of reality midway and fall back into the stage of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha;
or will he proceed toward unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment and be able to bring benefit and happiness to all beings until the end of the future?"
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells securely in the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), at that time Māra the Evil One gives rise to great sorrow and suffering, his body and mind trembling as if pierced by a poisoned arrow."
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), at that time Māra the Evil One comes to his presence and manifests various terrifying things—namely, swords and blades, wild beasts, venomous snakes, and fierce fires blazing forth from all four directions—with the intent to cause the bodhisattva’s body and mind to be struck with alarm and fear, to lose the resolve for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), and to cause his mind to become despondent regarding the practice he is engaged in, even to the point of giving rise to a single thought of distraction, thereby obstructing unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening; such is the deep-seated wish of that evil Māra."
At that time, Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
"When all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom, are they all disturbed by evil Māras, or are there some who are disturbed and others who are not?"
The Buddha told Ānanda:

"It is not the case that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are disturbed and distracted by Māra when they practice the perfection of wisdom; rather, there are those who are disturbed and those who are not."
The Venerable Ānanda again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Which bodhisattva mahāsattvas, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, are disturbed and distracted by evil māras?”
“What kind of bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), is not disturbed by Māra?
The Buddha told Ānanda:

“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having heard the teaching of the profound perfection of wisdom in previous lives, lacked faith and understanding, and instead disparaged and slandered it, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva, when practicing the perfection of wisdom, will be disturbed by Māra.”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having heard the teaching of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* in previous lives, possesses a mind of faith and understanding and does not give rise to disparagement, then when this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the *prajñāpāramitā*, they will not be disturbed or confused by Māra.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing this teaching of the profound perfection of wisdom, should harbor doubt and hesitation as to whether it exists or does not exist, or whether it is real or unreal;
When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), he will be disturbed and distracted by Māra.

However, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva, upon hearing such a profound exposition of the perfection of wisdom, has no doubt or hesitation at all in his mind and is certain that it truly exists, then when this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he will not be disturbed or distracted by Māra.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is far removed from virtuous friends and is influenced by evil friends, they will not hear the profound meaning of the *prajñāpāramitā*. Because they do not hear it, they cannot comprehend it; because they do not comprehend it, they cannot practice it; and because they do not practice it, they cannot inquire:
'How should one practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā*?'"
"How should one train in the profound perfection of wisdom?
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they will be disturbed and distracted by Māra, the Evil One."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva associates with virtuous friends and is not influenced by evil friends, they will hear the profound meaning of the *prajñāpāramitā*. Because they have heard it, they are able to understand it; because they have understood it, they are able to practice it; and because they have practiced it, they are able to inquire:
"How should one practice the profound *prajñāpāramitā*?"
How should one train in the profound *prajñāpāramitā*?
When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the *prajñāpāramitā*, they shall not be disturbed or distracted by Māra.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva distances himself from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) and instead embraces and praises what is not the true, sublime Dharma, then while that bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he will be disturbed and distracted by Māra, the Evil One."

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva draws near to the perfection of wisdom and does not embrace or praise that which is not the true, sublime Dharma, then when this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they will not be disturbed or distracted by Māra.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva remains far removed from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they will disparage and slander the sublime and true Dharma."
At that time, Māra the Evil One thought to himself:

"Now this bodhisattva is my ally; because he slanders the sublime and true Dharma, there will arise immeasurable numbers of novice bodhisattvas who have newly entered the Mahāyāna and will likewise slander the sublime and true Dharma. By this cause and condition, my wish shall be fulfilled."

"Although there are immeasurable newly initiated bodhisattvas of the Mahāyāna who are my companions, they cannot fulfill my vows; yet this bodhisattva, as my companion, causes all my aspirations to be fulfilled. Therefore, this bodhisattva is my true companion, and I should embrace him so that his power may increase."
"When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they are then disturbed by evil Māras.

However, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva draws near to the perfection of wisdom, praises and accepts the true, sublime Dharma, and likewise causes immeasurable newly trained bodhisattvas of the Great Vehicle to praise and accept the true, sublime Dharma, then because of this, the evil Māras become sorrowful, anxious, and terrified; thus, when this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they are not disturbed by evil Māras."
"Furthermore, Ānanda!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when hearing the profound sūtras spoken on the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), should speak as follows:

'This principle of the perfection of wisdom is so profound, difficult to see, and difficult to realize; what is the use of proclaiming it, listening to it, receiving and upholding it, reading and reciting it, contemplating it, diligently practicing and studying it, or copying and disseminating it?'"
"I cannot even fathom the source or the bottom of this sūtra, let alone others of meager merit and shallow wisdom!

At that time, there were immeasurable newly initiated bodhisattvas of the Mahāyāna who, upon hearing what was said, were all struck with fear and alarm; they then retreated from the mind set on unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment and fell into the stages of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.
When these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), they are then disturbed and distracted by Māra.
If, when hearing the teaching of the profound sūtras of the perfection of wisdom, a bodhisattva-mahāsattva speaks thus:

"The principle of this perfection of wisdom is so profound that it is difficult to see and difficult to realize; if it were not proclaimed, heard, accepted, recited, contemplated, diligently practiced, written down, and disseminated, it would be impossible to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

At that time, there were immeasurable newly initiated bodhisattvas of the Mahāyāna who, hearing what was said, rejoiced and leaped for joy. They then constantly delighted in hearing, receiving, upholding, reading, and reciting the *Prajñāpāramitā*; they mastered it thoroughly, reflected upon it according to the principle, practiced it with diligence, expounded it for others, and transcribed and disseminated it, seeking to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. When these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice the *Prajñāpāramitā*, they are not disturbed or distracted by evil Māras.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on his own merits and roots of goodness, looks down upon other bodhisattva mahāsattvas, saying:
'I am able to abide in the practice of true seclusion, whereas you all lack it. "
"I am able to practice true detachment, whereas you are not.
At that time, the evil Māra rejoiced and leaped for joy, saying:
"This bodhisattva is my companion; he will wander through birth and death with no time of escape."

Why is this? Because these bodhisattvas rely on their own merit and roots of goodness to disparage other bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; they thus distance themselves from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment and are unable to apply themselves with diligence to purifying their own spheres.
When such a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they will be disturbed and distracted by Māra.

However, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not rely on their own meritorious roots of goodness to disparage other bodhisattva mahāsattvas, and although they constantly exert themselves in practicing all wholesome dharmas, they do not cling to the marks of those wholesome dharmas, then that bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, will not be disturbed or distracted by Māra.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, relying on his own name and lineage as well as the merits of the dhūta practices he has cultivated, treats with contempt other bodhisattvas who are cultivating superior wholesome dharmas; if he constantly praises himself and disparages others, falsely claiming that he possesses the actual practices, marks, and signs of a non-retrogressive bodhisattva mahāsattva when he does not; and if he gives rise to various afflictions, saying:
'You all lack the name and lineage of a bodhisattva, whereas I alone possess them.'"
Because they disparage other bodhisattvas out of overweening pride,
at that time Māra the Evil One becomes greatly delighted and thinks to himself:
"Now this bodhisattva will ensure that my realm and palaces are not empty, thereby increasing the populations of the hells, the animal realm, and the realm of hungry ghosts."

At that time, the evil Māra assists him with his supernatural power, causing his majesty, influence, and eloquence to increase further. Consequently, many people believe and accept his words; because of this, they are exhorted and incited to share in those same evil views. Having shared in those evil views, they follow that false learning; having followed that false learning, their afflictions blaze up intensely. Because their minds are inverted, all the physical, verbal, and mental karma they initiate are capable of bringing about undesirable, ruinous, and painful results.

By this causal condition, the realms of hell, the animal kingdom, and the world of hungry ghosts increase, causing the palaces and lands of Māra to become filled; consequently, the evil Māra rejoices and leaps for joy, and all his undertakings proceed according to his will with complete mastery. Thus, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, they are disturbed and distracted by that evil Māra.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not rely on their own false name and title nor on the merits of the dhūta practices they have cultivated to disparage other bodhisattvas who are practicing superior wholesome dharmas; if they remain free from pride regarding their own virtues, never praising themselves or slandering others, and are able to skillfully recognize the deeds of Māra, then when this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they will not be disturbed or distracted by Māra.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva mutually disparages, quarrels with, and slanders those who seek the vehicles of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, at that time the evil Māra, having seen this, thinks:

'Although this bodhisattva is far from unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, he is not extremely far; although he is near to the realms of hell, animals, and hungry ghosts, he is not very near.'"
Having formed this thought, although he felt joy, he did not leap for it.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva and other bodhisattva mahāsattvas mutually disparage, quarrel, and slander one another, at that time the evil Māra, seeing this occurrence, thinks:
"These two bodhisattvas are extremely far from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment and are very close to the realms of hell, animals, and hungry ghosts."

Having formed this thought, he rejoices and leaps for joy, increasing his own power and influence to cause the two factions to contend without ceasing, and to make the remaining immeasurable and boundless sentient beings develop a deep-seated revulsion toward the Mahāyāna; when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) in this manner, he is then disturbed and distracted by Māra, the Evil One.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not disparage, quarrel with, or slander those who seek the vehicles of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but instead employs skillful means to guide them toward the Mahāyāna, or causes them to diligently cultivate the superior virtues of their own respective vehicles; and if they likewise do not disparage, quarrel with, or slander those sons of good family who seek unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, but instead mutually instruct one another in the cultivation of superior wholesome dharmas so that they may swiftly attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and turn the wondrous wheel of Dharma to deliver the multitudes of sentient beings—then this bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, will not be disturbed by Māra.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has not yet received the prediction of non-retrogression for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment should give rise to a harmful mind toward those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have received the prediction of non-retrogression for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment—engaging in strife, disparagement, abuse, or slander—that bodhisattva mahāsattva, in accordance with the number of such thoughts of non-benefit that arise, shall retrogress from the sublime practices cultivated over as many eons; for that same duration, they shall remain far removed from virtuous friends and undergo the bonds of birth and death for that same length of time."

If one does not abandon the great bodhicitta, then for as many eons as were previously mentioned, one shall don the armor of the great vow and diligently cultivate sublime practices without interruption; only then will the lost merit be restored.
At that time, Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:

"Regarding the suffering of the cycle of birth and death resulting from the evil thoughts generated by these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, must they necessarily wander through saṃsāra for such a duration, or can they also attain liberation in the interim?"

Regarding the superior practices from which these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have regressed: must they diligently exert themselves for that many eons, donning the armor of the great vow and practicing all superior deeds without interruption, before they can restore the merits they have lost? Or does the restoration of their original state occur in the interim?
The Buddha told Ānanda:
“I have taught for bodhisattvas, pratyekabuddhas, and śrāvakas the dharma of expiating transgressions and restoring one’s virtue.
Ānanda, you should know this!”

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has not yet received the prediction of non-retrogression for unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment conceives a harmful mind toward those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have received the prediction of non-retrogression for unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment—engaging in strife, disparagement, insult, or slander—and subsequently, lacking shame and remorse, harbors malice without relinquishing it, and is unable to confess and repent according to the Dharma.

I say that for such individuals, there is no possibility of emerging from their transgressions or restoring their virtue during that interval; they must instead wander through birth and death for that many eons, bound by manifold sufferings and far removed from virtuous friends.

If one does not abandon the great bodhicitta, but dons the armor of the great vow for that many eons, diligently cultivating sublime practices without interruption, only then will one restore the merits that had declined.

"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has not yet received the prediction of non-retrogression for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment should give rise to a harmful mind toward those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have received the prediction of non-retrogression for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment—engaging in strife, disparagement, humiliation, or slander—and subsequently feels shame and remorse, binds no further evil, and is immediately able to confess and repent according to the Dharma, thinking:
'I have now obtained this human body so difficult to find; how could I allow such faults and evils to arise again and lose this great, wholesome benefit?'"
I ought to benefit all sentient beings; how could I allow myself to cause them harm instead?
I ought to revere all sentient beings as a servant serves his master; how could I allow myself to give rise to arrogance, to insult, or to despise them instead?
I ought to endure all the beatings and verbal abuse of sentient beings; how could I permit myself to retaliate against them with violent or wicked deeds and words?
I ought to reconcile all sentient beings so that they may respect and love one another; how could I permit myself to again give rise to harsh speech and engage in conflict with them?
I ought to endure being trodden upon by all sentient beings for a long time, like a road or a bridge; how could I allow myself to respond to them with contempt or insult?

I seek unexcelled, perfect enlightenment in order to uproot the great suffering of birth and death for sentient beings and enable them to attain ultimate peace and happiness in nirvana; how could I possibly wish to inflict further suffering upon them?
From this day forth until the end of the future, I shall be like one who is dull-witted, mute, deaf, and blind, making no conceptual distinctions regarding any sentient beings.

Even if one were to sever their head, feet, arms, gouge out their eyes, cut off their ears, slice off their nose, cut out their tongue, or saw apart every limb and member of their body, they would never give rise to malice toward that sentient being.

If I give rise to evil, I shall then fall away and destroy the mind of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment that I have generated; I shall obstruct the sought-after knowledge of all modes and be unable to benefit and bring peace and happiness to sentient beings.

Ānanda, you should know that for these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, I say there is also the meaning of emerging from transgression and restoring their goodness even during the interim; it is not necessary for them to undergo the cycle of birth and death for as many eons as that.
Māras will be unable to disturb them, and they will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"Furthermore, Ānanda!

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should not engage in social interaction with those who seek the vehicle of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas; even if they do engage in such interaction, they should not dwell together with them; and even if they do dwell together, they should not engage them in debate or formal analysis of the Dharma."
Why is this? If one were to engage in debate or definitive analysis with such individuals, they might give rise to thoughts of anger and resentment, or cause coarse and malicious speech to emerge.

However, Bodhisattvas should not give rise to thoughts of anger and resentment toward sentient beings, nor should they utter coarse or malicious speech; even if their head, feet, or limbs were to be severed, they should not give rise to anger or evil words.
Why is this? All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should form this thought:

"I seek unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment in order to uproot the manifold sufferings of birth and death for sentient beings and to enable them to attain ultimate benefit and peace; how could I possibly turn such an aim into an evil deed?"
"Ānanda, you should know this:

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to a mind of anger toward sentient beings and utters harsh and evil words, they will obstruct unexcelled, perfect enlightenment and also destroy the boundless dharmas of the bodhisattva practice."
Therefore, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who wish to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment should not harbor anger toward sentient beings, nor should they utter harsh or evil speech.
At that time, Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying,
“How should bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell together with other bodhisattva-mahāsattvas?
The Buddha told Ānanda:
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, when dwelling together with other bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, should regard one another as they would the Great Teacher. Why is this?
When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas look at one another, they should form this thought:”

"He is our true spiritual friend; he is our companion, sharing the same vessel, traveling the same path, heading toward the same destination, and engaged in the same activity. In our training, our precepts, and the dharmas we study—whether through this training or that—all are without distinction."
Again, he reflects:
"Those bodhisattvas teach us the path to great enlightenment; they are my good companions and my teachers.

However, if those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell in distracted mental attention and remain far removed from mental attention associated with the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), I shall not train in the same way as they."
If those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas remain free from distracted attention and do not depart from attention associated with the knowledge of all modes, I shall always train therein in emulation of them.

"Ānanda, you should know that if a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they will swiftly bring the provisions for awakening to full completion, quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, and remain free from obstacles and difficulties throughout that interval."
Chapter 25: On Swift Action, Part One. At that time, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of exhaustion, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of non-arising, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of cessation, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of non-arising, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of non-existence, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of detachment, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of detachment from defilements, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of space, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of the dharma-realm, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains for the sake of nirvāṇa, is this training in the knowledge of all modes?
The Buddha told Subhūti:
"When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, he does not train in the knowledge of all aspects.
The Venerable Subhūti again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"For what reason, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, does he not train in the knowledge of all aspects?
The Buddha told Subhūti:
"What do you think?"

Since the Buddha has realized the ultimate perfection of suchness, he is called the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha; can this suchness be said to be exhausted, and so on, up to being said to be nirvāṇa?
Subhūti replied,
“No, World-Honored One!”
Why is this? Because True Suchness is free from characteristics and cannot be fully described, even to the point that it cannot be described as nirvāṇa.
The Buddha told Subhūti:
"Therefore, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are not training for the sake of the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvajñajñāna*).

Subhūti, you should know that if a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not train for the sake of exhaustion, they are training for the knowledge of all aspects; even if they do not train for the sake of nirvāṇa, they are training for the knowledge of all aspects."

Why is this? Because the Buddha has realized the ultimate perfection of suchness, he is called the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha; at that time, he realizes the suchness of the knowledge of all modes, which is inexhaustible even unto nirvāṇa.
Therefore, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are training in the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*).

Subhūti, you should know that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are training in the skillful means of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā-upāyakauśalya*); they are training in the stage of a Buddha; they are training in the ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and other immeasurable and boundless Buddha-qualities. This constitutes having already trained in the knowledge of all modes.
“Subhūti, you should know that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they reach the ultimate perfection of all training.
Subhūti, you should know!”
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, no devas, māras, or any followers of external paths can subdue them.
"Suvikrāntavikrāmin, you should know this!"
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they swiftly attain the non-retrogressive nature of a bodhisattva.
Subhūti, you should know that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they swiftly abide on the stage of a bodhisattva’s non-retrogression.
“Subhūti, you should know that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they will swiftly sit upon the sublime seat of awakening.
Subhūti, you should know!”
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they practice the sphere of activity of their ancestral Tathāgatas. Subhūti, you should know that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way,
they have already trained in the Dharma that serves as a refuge and protection for all sentient beings, because this training is the nature of great loving-kindness and great compassion.
"Subhūti, you should know that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are training in the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma with its three turnings and twelve aspects."

"Subhūti, you should know that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are training to establish hundreds of thousands of koṭis of sentient beings in the ultimate peace and happiness of nirvāṇa."
“Subhūti, you should know that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are training to ensure that the lineage of the Tathāgatas is never interrupted.
Subhūti, you should know that...”
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are training in the opening of the gate of the deathless by all Buddhas.
"Subhūti, you should know that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are training in establishing immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings in the three vehicles."

“Subhūti, you should know that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they are training to manifest the ultimate, quiescent, and truly unconditioned realm of all sentient beings; this is the training for the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna).”
“Subhūti, you should know that those who train in this manner are not able to be trained by inferior sentient beings. Why is that?

One who trains in this manner desires to skillfully rescue all sentient beings from the great suffering of birth and death; desires to skillfully establish all sentient beings in vast and supreme matters; desires to share with sentient beings the ultimate benefit and peace; desires to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment together with sentient beings; and desires to train in the sublime practice of benefiting oneself and others together with sentient beings, as inexhaustible and uninterrupted as the great void of space.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they will certainly not fall into any of the hells, the animal realm, the realm of hungry ghosts, or among the asuras; they will certainly not be born in border regions or among the barbarians (mleccha); they will certainly not be born into the families of caṇḍālas, of pukkasas, or into any other various families that are impoverished, lowly, or lacking in moral discipline; and they will certainly not be born into families of various craftsmen, musicians, merchants, or those of impure livelihoods."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, wherever he is born, he will never be blind, deaf, mute, crippled, or have impaired sense faculties; he will not be hunchbacked, epileptic, afflicted with abscesses, scabies, leprosy, hemorrhoids, or malignant sores; he will be neither too tall nor too short, nor will he be dark-skinned, nor will he suffer from various foul and loathsome diseases."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, in every birth they will always obtain a complete retinue, complete faculties, and complete limbs; their voice will be clear and resonant, their physical appearance dignified and handsome, and their speech will be majestic and solemn, such that all people love and respect them."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, in whatever place they are born, they abstain from taking life, abstain from taking what is not given, abstain from sexual misconduct, abstain from false speech, abstain from harsh speech, abstain from divisive speech, and abstain from frivolous speech; they also abstain from covetousness, ill will, and wrong views. They never embrace false and deviant dharmas, nor do they sustain their lives through deviant dharmas, nor do they accept as friends those sentient beings who break the precepts, hold evil views, or slander the Dharma."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they will never be reborn in the long-lived heavens of the gods who delight in pleasure and possess little wisdom."

Why is this? Because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have accomplished the power of skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*); by virtue of this power of skillful means, although they are able to repeatedly enter the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), and the formless attainments (*ārūpya-samāpatti*), they do not undergo rebirth under the influence of those states.

Because they are sustained by the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they achieve such skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*) that, although they constantly attain mastery in entering and emerging from all meditative absorptions (*samādhi*), they do not follow the power of those absorptions to be reborn in the long-lived heavens (*dīrghāyuṣka-deva*), thereby neglecting the practice of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva path.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they attain pure power, pure fearlessness, and pure buddha-dharmas."
The Venerable Subhūti then addressed the Buddha, saying:

"If all phenomena are pure by their very nature, how is it that when bodhisattva-mahāsattvas train in this way, they are further able to realize the pure powers, the pure fearlessnesses, and the pure buddha-dharmas?"
The Buddha told Subhūti: “So it is! So it is!”
It is as you have said:
all phenomena are by their very nature pure from the beginning.

Within this fundamental purity of all phenomena, the bodhisattva mahāsattva diligently trains in the profound *prajñāpāramitā* through skillful means; thus, they penetrate reality as it is, with a mind that neither sinks nor is obstructed, remaining far removed from all afflictions and attachments.

Therefore, it is said that when a bodhisattva trains in this manner, they further attain purity regarding all phenomena; by virtue of these causes and conditions, they obtain the power of purity, the fearlessness of purity, and the pure Buddha-dharmas.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
Although the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is pure, ordinary beings do not know, see, or realize this.
Desiring to cause them to know, see, and realize it, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas exert diligent effort and practice the perfection of wisdom with skillful means, forming this thought:"

"Having known, seen, and awakened to the original purity of all phenomena, I have brought all sentient beings to such authentic realization, enabling them likewise to know, see, and awaken to the original purity of all phenomena."
"When this bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they attain the power of purity, the fearlessness of purity, and the pure Buddha-dharmas.
Furthermore, Subhūti!"

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, they are able to penetrate the various mental activities of all sentient beings and reach the ultimate further shore; through skillful means, they cause all sentient beings to know that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is pure, thereby enabling them to realize the ultimately cool state of nirvāṇa.
The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Fascicle 552; The Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra,
Fascicle 553.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang under Imperial Order.
Part Four, Chapter Twenty-five, "The Swift," Section Two: "Subhūti, you should know this:

for example, on the great earth, precious things such as gold and silver are produced in few places, whereas saline and alkaline substances are produced in many places. It is the same with all sentient beings: few study the Prajñāpāramitā, while many study the dharmas of the stages of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas."
Subhūti, you should know this:

for example, among those in the human realm, only a few are able to perform the karma of a universal monarch (cakravartin), while the majority are able to perform the karma of various minor kings; so it is with all sentient beings—only a few are able to cultivate the path to the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna), while the majority are able to cultivate the paths of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
Subhūti, you should know this!

For example, among the gods who dwell on the earth in the desire realm, only a few are able to perform the karma for Śakra, Lord of the Devas, while the majority are able to perform the karma for the other classes of gods; so it is with all sentient beings: few seek unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, while many seek the fruits of the vehicles of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
"Subhūti, you should know this!

For example, within the first dhyāna of the form realm, only a small portion is able to cultivate the karma of a Great Brahmā King, while the vast majority are able to cultivate the karma of the Brahmā assembly; so it is with all sentient beings: only a few attain non-retrogression from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, while the many still undergo retrogression from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

"Therefore, Subhūti! Among all classes of sentient beings, only a small fraction are able to give rise to the mind of great enlightenment (*mahābodhicitta*). Among them, even fewer are able to cultivate the conduct of a bodhisattva mahāsattva. Among them, even fewer are able to train in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*). Among them, even fewer are able to employ skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*) regarding the perfection of wisdom. Among them, those who attain non-retrogression from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi*) are extremely few."
Therefore, Subhūti,

if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to be counted among the very few sentient beings, they should diligently practice and study the profound perfection of wisdom through skillful means, so as to attain non-retrogression from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way in the profound perfection of wisdom through skillful means, they do not give rise to a mind associated with discord, a mind associated with doubt, a mind associated with stinginess, a mind associated with transgression of the precepts, a mind associated with anger and resentment, a mind associated with laziness, a mind associated with distraction, or a mind associated with faulty wisdom."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way in the profound perfection of wisdom through skillful means, they are able to encompass all perfections, gather all perfections, and lead all perfections."
Why is this? Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* contains all *pāramitās*.
Subhūti, you should know this!

Just as the false view of a self-body can universally encompass all sixty-two views, so too is it with the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), which contains and sustains all perfections (pāramitās).
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to correctly train in the profound perfection of wisdom through skillful means, they can cause all the perfections to be drawn forth and gradually increase.
"Subhūti, you should know that just as the life-faculty sustains all the other faculties, so too does the profound perfection of wisdom sustain all supreme wholesome dharmas."
Why is this? If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to correctly practice and study the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they are universally able to uphold all wholesome dharmas.
"Subhūti, you should know this!
Just as when the life-faculty ceases, all other faculties follow in cessation, so it is with the profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva falls away from such profound perfection of wisdom, they fall away from all wholesome dharmas."
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to correctly practice and study the profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they will be able to universally eliminate all unwholesome dharmas.
Therefore, Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to reach the ultimate further shore of all pāramitās, they should diligently practice and study the profound prajñāpāramitā.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can diligently study and practice the profound perfection of wisdom, they are the most supreme and most excellent among all sentient beings."
Why is this? It is because these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are able to diligently practice and study the unsurpassed Dharma of the profound *prajñāpāramitā*.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!"
"What do you think?
Are the sentient beings in this trichiliocosm many?
Subhūti replied:
"The sentient beings within Jambudvīpa alone are already countless; how much more so must those in the trichiliocosm not be numerous!"
The Buddha told Subhūti: "So it is! So it is!"
"It is as you have said.
Subhūti, you should know that even if all the sentient beings in a trichiliocosm were to simultaneously obtain human bodies, neither before nor after one another."

Having attained human birth, they all, neither before nor after one another, will give rise to the mind of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and cultivate the practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Once their cultivation is perfected, they all, neither before nor after one another, will attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.

There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, for as long as their lives last, are able to provide offerings of exquisite clothing, food and drink, dwellings, bedding, medicinal requisites for illness, and various material wealth to these Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, honoring, revering, respecting, and praising them.
"What do you think?
By reason of this cause and condition, would that bodhisattva mahāsattva acquire much merit?
Subhūti replied:
"Very much so,
World-Honored One!
Very much so!"
“Excellent, Sugata!
The Buddha told Subhūti:
“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can cultivate such profound prajñāpāramitā, the merit obtained in the mere twinkling of an eye far exceeds that of the former, being immeasurable and incalculable.”

Why is this? Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* possesses great purpose and function, enabling the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas to swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Therefore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening; wishes to be the foremost among all sentient beings; wishes to universally benefit all sentient beings; wishes to act as a protector for those without protection, a refuge for those without refuge, a resort for those without a resort, eyes for those without eyes, and light for those without light; and wishes to show the correct path to those who have lost it, and to lead those who have not attained nirvāṇa to attain it—such a one should train in this profound perfection of wisdom.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to practice the sphere of activity traversed by all buddhas, wishes to dwell in the exalted position of the Great Sages that all buddhas occupy,
wishes to sport in the places where all buddhas sport, and wishes to act as a great lion among all buddhas— "
Hūṃ! Desiring to strike the unsurpassed Dharma-drum of all Buddhas, desiring to strike the unsurpassed Dharma-bell of all Buddhas,
desiring to blow the unsurpassed Dharma-conch of all Buddhas, desiring to ascend the unsurpassed Dharma-throne of all Buddhas,
desiring to expound the unsurpassed Dharma-meaning of all Buddhas, desiring to sever the net of doubts of all sentient beings, desiring to enter the [assembly] of all Buddhas...
If you wish to receive the subtle and wondrous Dharma-bliss of all Buddhas within the nectar-like Dharma-realm; if you wish to realize the perfect and pure merits of all Buddhas;

and if you wish to proclaim the True Dharma for all sentient beings throughout the trichiliocosm with a single voice, universally causing all to obtain great benefit—you should study this profound Prajñāpāramitā.
"Furthermore, Subhūti,
if a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices and studies this profound perfection of wisdom in this way, there is no mundane or supramundane merit or excellence that they will not attain."
Why is this? Because the profound perfection of wisdom is the locus upon which all kinds of merit and roots of goodness depend.
Subhūti, you should know this!
I have never seen a bodhisattva mahāsattva who, by diligently practicing such profound prajñāpāramitā, failed to attain the superior merits and benefits of both the mundane and supramundane realms.
At that time, Subhūti addressed the Buddha, saying:
"When bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice and study this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, can they also attain the merits and roots of goodness of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas?"
The Buddha told Subhūti:

"The bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are also able to attain all the merits and roots of goodness of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; however, they neither dwell in nor cling to them. Having correctly observed them with superior wisdom and vision, they transcend the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas and enter the bodhisattva’s state of certainty and departure from birth."
There is no merit or root of goodness that these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cannot attain.

Furthermore, Subhūti, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should train themselves in all aspects of the merits and roots of goodness of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; although they do not seek to realize them for themselves, they desire to master them thoroughly so as to proclaim and reveal them to those sentient beings.
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they draw near to the knowledge of all modes, will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and will be able to bring benefit and happiness to all beings throughout the future."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this way, they become a truly pure field of merit for all the world—including its devas, humans, and asuras—surpassing the fields of merit of all the world’s śramaṇas, brahmins, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas, and swiftly attaining the knowledge of all modes."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in this manner, wherever they are born, they do not abandon this profound perfection of wisdom, they do not depart from this profound perfection of wisdom, and they constantly practice this profound perfection of wisdom."
"Furthermore, Subhūti!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can practice such profound *prajñāpāramitā*, you should know that they have attained non-retrogression regarding all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), are able to correctly awaken to all phenomena, have distanced themselves from the levels of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and are drawing near to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Furthermore, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they might form such a thought:
'This is the perfection of wisdom; this is the time of cultivation; this is the place of cultivation.'"

"I am able to cultivate this profound *prajñāpāramitā*; by means of such profound *prajñāpāramitā*, I shall abandon those dharmas that ought to be abandoned, and I shall be able to bring forth the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*)."
This bodhisattva mahāsattva is not practicing the perfection of wisdom, nor can they comprehend the perfection of wisdom. Why is this?
The profound *prajñāpāramitā* does not form such thoughts as:

"I am the *prajñāpāramitā*; this is the time of cultivation; this is the place of cultivation; this is the cultivator; these are the phenomena from which the *prajñāpāramitā* is detached; these are the phenomena illuminated by the *prajñāpāramitā*; and this is the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment realized by the *prajñāpāramitā*."
"If one knows in this way, that is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Subhūti,
when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the profound perfection of wisdom, they form this thought:"

"This is not the perfection of wisdom; this is not the time for cultivation; this is not the place for cultivation; this is not the cultivator. It is not by means of the perfection of wisdom that one distances oneself from all dharmas that should be abandoned, nor is it by means of the perfection of wisdom that one realizes unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
Why is this? It is because all phenomena abide in suchness without distinction.
Subhūti, you should know this!
"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva makes no conceptual distinctions regarding any phenomena and has no cognitive apprehension of them, this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.
Chapter 26: The Parable of the Illusion, Part Four At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, had this thought:
"If a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom already surpasses all classes of sentient beings, how much more so when they attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment!"

If sentient beings, upon hearing the name of the knowledge of all modes, develop deep faith and understanding, they will already obtain the excellent benefits of human existence and attain the most supreme lifespan in the world; how much more so for those who resolve their minds toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, or who are able to hear this profound *prajñāpāramitā*!

If any sentient beings are able to resolve upon unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment and hear this profound sūtra of the *Prajñāpāramitā*, all other sentient beings should aspire to rejoice in them; the merit they thereby obtain cannot be equaled by any in the world, including devas, humans, or asuras.
At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing the thoughts in the mind of Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed him, saying: "So it is! So it is!"
"It is as you have thought.

At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, leaped for joy and transformed himself into celestial *sūkṣmasvara* flowers, which he held up and scattered over the Tathāgata and the various bodhisattvas. Having scattered the flowers, he made this aspiration:

“If sons of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle seek to proceed toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, by means of the roots of goodness and merit born from me, may their excellent aspirations and merits be swiftly fulfilled; may the unsurpassed Buddha-dharmas they seek be swiftly fulfilled; may all the dharmas associated with the knowledge of all modes that they seek be swiftly fulfilled; may the dharmas of self-mastery they seek be swiftly fulfilled; may the untainted noble dharmas they seek be swiftly fulfilled; and may everything they wish to hear of the Dharma be attained according to their wishes.”
"If there are those who seek the vehicle of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, may their aspirations also be swiftly fulfilled.
Having made this vow, he addressed the Buddha, saying:

"If there are sons of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who have already resolved upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, I shall never give rise to even a single thought of a contrary intention to cause them to retreat from the mind of great bodhi."

I shall never give rise to even a single thought of divergent intent that would cause the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas to become weary of unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, or to fall back into the stages of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas;
I shall never give rise to even a single thought of divergent mind that would cause the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas to lose the mental engagement associated with great compassion.

If Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas have already developed a deep-seated aspiration for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, I vow that their resolve shall increase even further so that they may swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment;

and I vow that these Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, having witnessed the various sufferings within saṃsāra, shall give rise to various firm and great vows out of a desire to bring benefit and happiness to the world of devas, humans, asuras, and others, saying:
"Having myself crossed the great ocean of saṃsāra, I shall also diligently strive to deliver those who have not yet been delivered."
Since I have already liberated myself from the fetters of birth and death, I shall also diligently strive to liberate those who are not yet liberated;
since I have already attained peace and security amidst the various terrors of birth and death, I shall also diligently strive to bring peace and security to those who have not yet found it;
and since I have already realized ultimate *nirvāṇa* for myself, I shall also diligently strive to cause all others who have not yet realized it to likewise attain it.
“World-Honored One!
If there are sentient beings who, with a profound mind, rejoice in the merit of a bodhisattva who has first resolved to attain enlightenment, how much merit do they obtain?
And if they, with a profound mind, rejoice in the merit of a bodhisattva who has long since resolved to attain enlightenment and is practicing various sublime deeds, how much merit do they obtain?”
How much merit is obtained by rejoicing with a profound mind in the virtues of a bodhisattva on the stage of non-retrogression?
How much merit is obtained by rejoicing with a profound mind in the virtues of a bodhisattva bound to only one more birth?
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, the Lord of the Devas, saying: “Kauśika!
The number of Mount Sumeru, the king of mountains, may be known; however, the measure of the merit produced by the minds of these sentient beings through sympathetic joy cannot be known.”
Kauśika! While the number of the four great continents may be known, the measure of the merit produced by the minds of these sentient beings rejoicing together cannot be known.
Kauśika! While the number of small chiliocosms may be known, the measure of the merit produced by the minds of these sentient beings accompanied by sympathetic joy cannot be known.
Kauśika! While the number of two-thousandfold world systems may be known, the measure of the merit produced by the minds of these sentient beings rejoicing together cannot be known.
Kauśika! While the number of worlds in this trichiliocosm of mine may be known, the measure of the merit produced by the minds of these sentient beings through sympathetic joy cannot be known.

Kauśika! Suppose the trichiliocosm were merged into a single ocean; if one were to take a single hair, divide it into a hundred parts, and use the tip of one such part to dip into that ocean, the number of drops could be known. However, the measure of the merit produced by the minds of these sentient beings rejoicing together cannot be known.
At that time, Śakra, the Lord of Devas, again addressed the Buddha, saying:

“If there are sentient beings who do not give rise to sympathetic joy toward the immeasurable and boundless, supreme merits of Bodhisattvas—from their first generation of the mind of awakening until their realization of the sought-after unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment—or if they fail to hear of, know, recollect, or give sympathetic joy to the merit produced by the mind associated with such sympathetic joy, it should be known that they are all possessed by Māra, bewitched by Māra, partisans of Māra, or those who have passed away from the celestial realm of Māra and been reborn here.”

Why is this? If a bodhisattva mahāsattva seeks to attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment and cultivates the various practices of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, anyone who gives rise to a mind that deeply rejoices in those merits, or anyone who, with a profound mind, recollects those merits of rejoicing and gives rise to rejoicing, will all be able to destroy the palaces, retinues, and armies of all Māras; they will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and will be able to bring benefit and happiness to all beings throughout the future.
"Bhagavān!

If there are sentient beings who, with deep devotion, revere and love the Triple Gem of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, and who, wherever they are born, always desire to see the Buddha, hear the Dharma, and meet the Saṅgha; if they should deeply rejoice in the roots of virtue and merit of the assembly of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and having rejoiced, dedicate them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they should not give rise to the notion of duality or non-duality."
"If one can act in this way, one will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, benefiting sentient beings and destroying the hosts of Māra.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, King of the Devas, saying:
"It is so! It is so!"
So it is! It is just as you have said, Kauśika!

If any sentient beings, with a profound mind, rejoice in the roots of virtue and merit of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas and dedicate them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, those sentient beings will swiftly fulfill all the practices of a bodhisattva and quickly realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

“If there are sentient beings who, with a profound mind, rejoice in the roots of virtue and merit of the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and dedicate them toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, these sentient beings possess great power; they are always able to serve all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and spiritual friends, and they constantly hear the profound sūtras of the Prajñāpāramitā and skillfully understand their meaning and intent.”

These sentient beings, having accomplished such roots of merit through the virtue of sympathetic joy and dedication, will, in whatever place they are born, always be honored, revered, respected, and praised by all the worlds—gods, humans, and asuras. They shall not see unpleasant forms, hear unpleasant sounds, smell unpleasant odors, taste unpleasant flavors, experience unpleasant tactile sensations, or contemplate unwholesome dharmas. They shall not fall into evil realms, but will constantly experience various untainted, supreme joys among gods and humans. Never separated from the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, they shall travel from one Buddha-field to another, drawing near to the Buddhas, planting various roots of goodness, maturing sentient beings, and purifying Buddha-lands.
Why is this so, Kauśika?

It is because these sentient beings are able to rejoice with a profound mind in the roots of virtue and merit of the immeasurable bodhisattvas and dedicate them toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment; by means of these causes and conditions, their roots of virtue increase and they will swiftly realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Having attained unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, they are able to truly benefit immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless sentient beings until the end of the future, causing them to abide in the realm of nirvana without remainder.

"For this reason, Kauśika, sons of good family who abide in the Bodhisattva vehicle should, regarding the roots of goodness and merits of the assembly of bodhisattvas, rejoice in them all and dedicate them toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
